EventNotes:
Martha's Ride 2026 Benefiting The Martha Fund — Building Playgrounds Across Pittsburgh, Honoring Those Who Serve

Martha's Ride honors FBI Special Agent Martha Dixon, killed in the line of duty on November 22, 1994, and stands in support of the law enforcement community that shares her legacy. Inspired by the Police Unity Tour, this annual ride travels from her name on the National Law Enforcement Officers Memorial Wall in Washington, D.C. to the Martha Dixon FBI Field Office in Pittsburgh — 329 miles along the C&O Canal Towpath and Great Allegheny Passage. Every dollar raised builds playgrounds for Pittsburgh's kids in the communities our officers protect every day.

THREE WAYS TO RIDE

Endurance Ride — Sept 28–Oct 2 329 miles over five days. Depart the National Law Enforcement Officers Memorial Wall in Washington, D.C. on Monday, September 28 and finish at the Martha Dixon FBI Field Office in Pittsburgh on Friday, October 2. Overnight stops in Harper's Ferry, WV (Clarion Inn); Hancock, MD; Cumberland, MD (Fairfield Inn); and Ohiopyle, PA. A SAG vehicle and trailer accompany the full route with limited mechanical support, nutrition, and gear transport. Full-service bike shops are available along the route for serious mechanical issues. Riders arrange their own lodging — recommended accommodations provided at confirmation.

Pittsburgh Day Ride — Oct 3 (10-Mile) Start at Southside Riverfront Park under the Birmingham Bridge and roll out along the South Side trail. Sweeping views of the Pittsburgh skyline across the Monongahela make this one of the most scenic rides in the city — flat, welcoming, and perfect for families and first-timers. Finish at the Martha Dixon bench near Hot Metal Bridge where a Pittsburgh Police escort leads the group back down Carson Street to the park for the official finish. Open to all fitness levels. Bring the family.  

Due to an indefinite closure of the GAP trail between Duquesne and Homestead caused by unstable rock hazards, we have updated the 30-mile route. The 10-mile route remains unchanged.

Pittsburgh Day Ride — Oct 3 (30-Mile) Start at Southside Riverfront Park and head east on the GAP to the 1892 Batle of Homestead Pump House - Pittsburgh steel and labor history right on the water.   Return west, cross the Hot Metal Bridge, and pick up Three Rivers Heritage Trail past PNC Park Acrisure Stadium, and Point State Park where all three rivers meet.  Cross the Fort Duquesne Bridge, heading northeast along the Allegheny trough the Strip District and Lawrenceville to Millvale Riverfront Park and back. Finish at Hot Metal Bridge where the Pittsburgh Police escort leads everyone down Carson Street to the finish line.  The is Pittsburgh from two wheels. 

Garmin Route GPS - https://connect.garmin.com/app/course/508322936

RidewithGPS - https://ridewithgps.com/trips/408766151

Note: GPS Route takes you to the Police Escort meet-up.  The escort route is roughly 2.3 miles.  Subject to small changes based on the Police recommendation.  

AFTERPARTY All riders and supporters are invited to the afterparty at Burghers Brewing the Southside.  Riders, Family and Friends are all encouraged to come celebrate immediately following the ride.  Thank you to Baird Wealth Management for Sponsoring the afterparty! 

Sign up for our updates on the website.  

QUESTIONS Visit themarthafund.org or contact Connor Dixon at dixonc10@gmail.com.

EventNotes:
The Tour de Pines, sponsored by the Pinelands Alliance celebrates Pinelands Month in October.  The ride is co-sponsored by the Outdoor Club of South Jersey

This year we offer four single-day self-guided bicycle tours on the paved roads of the New Jersey Pinelands.  There is no other bike ride like this in New Jersey!

Participants register for each day & route they want to participate in; if you register for multiple days, you will automatically receive an entry fee discount on your additional days, if you register for them at the same time.  For example, your initial ride will cost $60, and your additional rides will cost $20 each.  Each of the first 200 participants will receive a complimentary Tour de Pines Ball Cap prior to your first ride (one per person, regardless of the numbers of days you register for). 

Proceeds benefit the Pineland Alliance (PPA).  Founded in 1989, the PPA is a private, nonprofit organization dedicated to saving the Pinelands of New Jersey.  PPA protects the land, water, plants, wildlife, and historic resources of New Jersey’s Pinelands National Reserve.  The PPA engages thousands of people each year in actions to protect the wildest place in New Jersey.

All routes start & finish in the same location; participants provide their own transportation, food, and lodging as these are unsupported rides.  Although the rides are self-supported & self-guided, we will provide each participant with:

  • Cue Sheets
  • GPS Files
  • Free Access to the Ride with GPS App
  • Instructions that contain details about the rides


Day 1: Thursday, October 1, 2026
RIDE LIKE THE DEVIL
Start/Finish location: Renault Winery, 72 North Bremen Avenue, Egg Harbor City, NJ 08215 

29 and 55-mile routes are available

This ride will take you to several historic and legendary sites in the Pine Barrens. The Long Route will visit Leeds Point – the birthplace of the Jersey Devil; other highlights include Port Republic and Oyster Creek, and side trips may be made to the Edwin B. Forsythe National Wildlife Refuge, Chestnut Neck (site of a battle fought in the Revolutionary War), places that are not too far off of the route. The short route follows the long route through some very dense and iconic areas within the pines. Pre-Ride Technical Support by Bikes by the Beach of Brigantine, NJ.
 

Day 2: Friday, October 2, 2026
WHITESBOG DISCOVERY
Start/Finish location: Whitesbog Village 120 W Whites Bogs Rd, Browns Mills, NJ 08015

26 and 52-mile routes are available

This ride departs from Historic Whitesbog Village, and travels through Greenwood Forest WMA,Chatsworth, Brendan Byrne State Forest, New Lisbon, Hanover Furnace, and Joint Base Fort Dix – McGuire.  It also passes Deborah Hospital and Mirror Lake in Browns Mills.  The long route gives riders an opportunity to stop at Pine Barrens landmark Hot Diggidy Dog in Chatsworth.  Pre-Ride Technical Support by Aistriu of Marlton, NJ. 


Day 3: Saturday, October 3, 2026
EDGE OF THE PINES
Start/Finish location: Parvin State Park 701 Almond Rd, Pittsgrove, NJ 08318

24, 34, and 51-mile routes are available

New for 2026, we take you to the Edge of the Pines, starting and finishing at Parvin State Park.  A hidden gem of the region the park combines rich history with abundant natural beauty.  This ride takes us further west than we’ve ventured before, past extensive stretches of farmland, and into small towns like Alloway and Elmer as we circle around Pittsgrove.

 

Day 4 – Sunday, October 4, 2026
BARREN BACKROADS
Start/Finish location: Pinelands Alliance 17 Pemberton Rd, Southampton NJ 08088

29 and 53-mile routes are available

Sunday’s ride departs from the Pinelands Alliance offices in Southampton, NJ, and winds through the scenic farm fields of Southampton before heading into Tabernacle and Chatsworth. Along the way, you’ll experience quiet back roads and long, straight stretches lined with towering pines.

The long route ventures into Chatsworth, the “Capital of the Pine Barrens” and the Cranberry Capital of New Jersey, where you’ll have a second opportunity to stop at the legendary Hot Diggidy Dog for a bite to eat. From there, you’ll continue to Tabernacle, where you’ll meet up with the short course, and you can choose to stop at either Nixon’s General Store or Russo’s Market—two well-known Pinelands establishments—for refreshments.

After taking in the area’s scenic farmland, the route heads back toward Southampton with a final stretch through the historic village of Vincentown before returning to the Pinelands Alliance.

As this ride serves as the Grand Finale of the 2026 Tour de Pines, we’re offering post-ride food & drinks within the Alliance’s renovated barn. Spellbound Brewing of Mount Holly, NJ provides beer for the post-ride festivities.  

Pre-Ride Technical Support by Erlton Bike Shop of Cherry Hill, NJ

 

Conditions of Entry:

  • All entries are final; no refunds. Entries are not transferable.  Please don't ask.
  • The first 200 individual registrants will receive a complimentary Tour de Pines Ball Cap
  • All merchandise orders and event premiums  (except special order jerseys) must be picked up at the event, including the Ball cap.
  • All participants are required to check in prior to each day’s ride. All participants must sign the event waiver and release during the registration process.  Parents/legal guardians must complete the waiver for minors.  All minors must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian at all times. 
     
  • The rides will be held rain or shine.  Normal amounts of rain will not cancel the rides.  However, in the event of Extreme Weather (such as named storms, or Official Weather Warning), other emergency, impassable roads, or other situations beyond the organizers’ control, the organizers reserve the right to cancel the event or reschedule it to a date of their convenience.  If you cannot attend the rescheduled date, entry fee refunds will not be issued.
  • Should the event be cancelled for reasons of force majeure, entry fees will not be refunded.
     
  • The roads are open to vehicular traffic; all rules of the road must be obeyed.  Participants are responsible for their own safety and for knowing and complying with New Jersey’s applicable laws and vehicle codes
  • Participants should ride in a safe and courteous manner; please stay to the right, except when passing.  NJ Traffic Guidelines suggest cyclists ride Single File.
  • All bicycles must have at least 1 working brake
  • All riders must wear a helmet that meets CPSC, ANSI and/or Snell (or similar standards).
  • Wearing headsets or earbuds are prohibited.
  • Bicycles with Aerobars are permitted, but use of aerobars while riding near others is prohibited due to safety concerns
  • Tandems are welcome, but each rider must register individually.
  • E-Bikes: Participants using Class 1 (Pedal Assist) & Class 2 (Pedal Assist w/ Throttle up to 20 MPH) E-Bikes are permitted to participate in the rides.  Use of Class 3 (Throttle Type >20 mph) and Class 4  E-Bikes (>750w) are prohibited from participating in the rides. E-Bike Users are required to be familiar with NJ E-Bike laws, and are solely responsible for their own compliance.  Please note that we may not be able to support or SAG large or heavy E-Bikes.  


    Support
    These are un-supported & self-guided rides.
  • Please carry food, beverages, spare tires, tubes, tools, etc.
  • There is no dedicated emergency medical transportation service for the event, please bring a cell phone and be prepared to dial 911 as needed.
  • The routes and road defects will NOT be marked.  Participants are responsible for their own navigation.  Access to Cue Sheets, RideWithGPS App and GPS files will be provided to the participants.

Race Format (3/6 Hour Race):

  • The rider who completes the most laps within the time limit (3 or 6 hours) will be declared the winner and will podium.
  • In the event of a tie, the fastest time to complete the tied number of laps will determine the winner.
  • If available, a scoreboard will be updated at the timing tent throughout the race.
  • A large digital clock at the finish line will display the remaining race time.
  • Laps completed after the time limit has expired will not be counted.
  • After completing a lap, riders may begin another lap, take a break or stop racing.
  • Completing at least one lap is required to avoid a DNF (Did Not Finish).
  • Riders may forfeit a lap at any time and return to the trailhead, but must report to the timing tent and inform race officials.
  • The race will begin in waves.
  • Wave size and start times will be determined by the Timing Officials.
  • Riders compete individually, teamwork is not allowed.

Race Format (Time Trial):

  • Individual Start – Riders start one at a time at set intervals (e.g., 30 sec or 1 min).
  • Course – Short trail course for XC. Pump track and Dual slalom courses are located near the trailhead.
  • Timing – Each rider is timed; fastest time wins.
  • Passing – Slower riders must yield if caught; good trail etiquette is essential.
  • Riders compete individually, teamwork is not allowed.

General XC Rules

  1. Equipment:
    • All riders must wear a bicycle helmet at all times while on the course. Failure to do so will result in disqualification.
    • Bikes must be mountain bikes suitable for off-road trails and equipped with a front and rear brake.
    • Race numbers must be visible on the handlebar area of the bike at all times.
  2. Conduct and Etiquette:
    • Racers must race respectfully and announce their intentions when passing another rider on the trail.
    • Cheating of any kind may result in disqualification at the discretion of the Timing Officials.
    • Abusive language, unsportsmanlike behavior, or deliberate obstruction of other riders will result in penalties or disqualification.
  3. Course Rules:
    • Riders must stay on the marked course at all times.
    • Cutting the course or taking shortcuts will result in disqualification.
    • If a rider encounters mechanical issues, they must move off the main trail to make repairs to avoid obstructing other participants.
  4. Safety:
    • Racers will be disqualified for racing without a bicycle helmet.
    • If a rider is seriously injured, the nearest rider must stop to offer assistance and report the incident to race officials. Call 911 if a rider is unconscious or unresponsive. 
    • For riders that have minor injuries, please inform the timing officials and we will send a representative onto the race course to assist. 
  5. Assistance and Support:
    • Racers may only receive assistance from non-racers in the staging area.
    • Racers may help other racers out on the course.
    • Racers are responsible for their own nutrition and hydration while on the course. Water will be available in the staging area.
  6. Penalties and Disqualification:
    • Timing Officials have the authority to disqualify racers for cheating, unsportsmanlike conduct, or safety violations.
    • Racers who intentionally cut the course or take shortcuts will be disqualified.
  7. Protests:
    • Any protests regarding race results or conduct must be filed with race officials within 30 minutes of the race ending.
    • Decisions made by race officials are final.
  8. Miscellaneous:
    • Please ensure that your race number is clearly visible on your bike at all times.
    • Good sportsmanship is expected of all participants. Unacceptable behavior will not be tolerated.

 

Enduro MTB Race Rules

  1. Race Format:
    • The race will be competed in stages with each stage being approximately one minute of “downhill” riding.
  2. Course Inspection:
    • Each rider will have pre-ride time to inspect the course before the race begins.
  3. Timed Runs:
    • Each rider may only receive one timed run per stage, unless otherwise approved by timing officials due to exceptional circumstances.
    • In case of interruption, such as stopping to assist a downed rider or mechanical issue, riders may reattempt a timed run. Riders must notify the Timing Official of the forfeited run to get approval for a reattempt. 
    • Reattempts for mechanical issues will be at the discretion of the race officials
  4. Assisting Downed Riders:
    • Riders are encouraged to check on and help downed riders.
    • If a rider stops to assist, they may have the opportunity to reattempt their timed run for that stage. The interruption must be reported to the Timing Official immediately.
  5. Safety:
    • Racers will be disqualified for racing without a bicycle helmet.
    • If a rider is seriously injured, the nearest rider must stop to offer assistance and report the incident to race officials. Call 911 if a rider is unconscious or unresponsive. 
    • For riders that have minor injuries, please inform the timing officials and we will send a representative onto the race course to assist. 
    • All riders must wear a helmet. Additional protective gear such as knee pads, elbow pads, and gloves are highly encouraged.
  6. Conduct:
    • Riders must act responsibly, showing good sportsmanship at all times.
    • Cheating, unsportsmanlike behavior, or any form of interference with other riders will result in penalties or disqualification.
  7. Course Rules:
    • Riders must stay on the marked course at all times.
    • Cutting the course or taking shortcuts will result in disqualification.
    • Mechanical issues must be resolved off the main trail to avoid interfering with other participants.
  8. Technical Assistance:
    • Riders may only receive assistance from non-racers in designated support areas.
    • Assistance with mechanical repairs from other riders on the course is permitted but must not interfere with other participants.
  9. Protests and Disqualification:
    • Any protests regarding race results or conduct must be filed with race officials within 30 minutes of the stage or race ending.
    • Decisions made by race officials are final.
    • Violations of the above rules will result in penalties or disqualification at the discretion of the race officials.

 

Ebike Rules for All Events

  1. Eligibility:
    • Only Class 1 Ebikes with a maximum of 750 watts and a 20 mph speed limiter are permitted unless otherwise agreed upon by vote from all participants.
  2. Motor Assistance:
    • Ebikes must be pedal assist only.
    • The motor cannot rely on a throttle to engage; it must assist the rider based on pedaling.
  3. Battery Rules:
    • The Ebike battery cannot be switched out during the event unless agreed upon by all participants to ensure fairness in battery consumption between different manufacturers and motor types.
    • Battery extenders are allowed on Ebikes with batteries under 500 watt-hours (wh).
    • Battery extenders and battery changes may be permitted for batteries over 500wh at the discretion of race officials, due to excessive reduction in battery capacity (e.g., old battery). This rule must also be agreed upon by all participants to account for the wide variety in bike manufacturers and battery types.
  4. Equipment and Safety:
    • All standard race rules and equipment requirements apply to Ebike riders, including mandatory helmet use and visible race numbers.
    • Riders must follow all course rules and remain on the designated trail.
  5. Conduct and Etiquette:
    • Ebike riders must race respectfully and announce their intentions when passing another rider on the trail.
    • Cheating or modifications to the Ebike to exceed the power or speed limits will result in disqualification.
  6. Technical Assistance:
    • Riders may only receive assistance from non-racers in the staging area.
    • Ebike riders may help other Ebike riders out on the course as long as it does not violate other rules.
  7. Protests and Disqualification:
    • Any violations of the above rules that give undue advantage, such as unauthorized battery changes or throttle use, will result in disqualification.
    • Rider protests regarding Ebike issues must be filed with race officials within 30 minutes of the race ending.
    • Decisions made by race officials are final.

REVISED MMBA ROUNDTABLE AGENDA 

Friday, October 2, 2026: Round table discussion

  • 9:00 AM – 9:30 AM | Check in BYOBreakfast and Networking
    • Location: Timber Ridge Banquet Hall
  • 9:20 AM – 9:30 AM | State of the Trails from MMBA Perspective: Opening Remarks
    • A brief overview of the current successes and hurdles facing Michigan mountain biking in 2026 and a glimpse of what we can work on for 2027. 
  • 9:30 AM – 12:30 AM | SWOT -MTB in MI 

Regional Chapter SWOT Evaluation

Strengths (Core Assets & Advantages)

Where is your chapter currently thriving?

  • Stewardship & Capacity: Do you have strong volunteer retention, active trail crews, and adequate trail maintenance equipment?
  • Land Manager Ties: Do you have solid working relationships with local DNR officials, US Forest Service managers, or county park boards?
  • Financial Health: Does the chapter maintain consistent local business sponsorships, fundraising events, or access to local grant dollars?
  • Community Engagement: Do you run well-attended group rides, skills clinics, or family-friendly events across diverse rider skill levels?
  • Local Land Manager Relationships: Strong ties with the DNR and local managers facilitate complex projects, like resolving wayfinding on the Vasa Singletrack or expanding regional trail networks.
  • Specialized Infrastructure Expertise: Chapters possess technical capacity for niche trail design, such as Adaptive MTB (aMTB) accessibility retrofits.
  • High Community Engagement: Dedicated volunteer bases drive trail maintenance, group rides, and social events (e.g., "No-Drop" and "Hammer" loops).
  • Grassroots Funding Mechanics: Capability to leverage local millages, corporate sponsorships, and state-level grants (such as the Michigan Natural Resources Trust Fund).

Weaknesses (Gaps & Operational Friction)

Where is your chapter struggling or stretched thin?

  • Administrative Burden: Are board members overwhelmed by managing member databases, manual dues processing, or individual insurance renewals?
  • Volunteer Burnout: Is maintenance heavily reliant on the same 3–5 core volunteers without a reliable succession plan?
  • Legacy Infrastructure: Are you spending excessive time managing unmapped social trails, poorly signed networks, or aging wooden features?
  • Demographic Reach: Does your trail network lack beginner-friendly loops or adaptive mountain bike (aMTB) infrastructure?
  • Maze-like Legacy Trails: Older trail networks suffer from poor signage, user confusion, and unmanaged "social trails" that require significant cleanup.
  • Resource Disparities: Regional chapters vary widely in access to funding, active volunteer hours, and local corporate sponsor bases.

 

External Factors (Statewide Alignment & Trends)

Opportunities (Growth & Expansion)

How can statewide partnership unlock local value?

  • LMB Integration: Will shifting administrative, database (CRM), and insurance management to the central LMB portal free up local leadership time?
  • Legislative Advocacy: How can centralized advocacy in Lansing help secure state funding (e.g., Michigan Natural Resources Trust Fund) for your chapter's local expansion plans? 
  • Inclusive Trail Building: Can retrofitting existing trails for Adaptive MTB (aMTB) attract new user groups and fresh grant funding?
  • Wayfinding & Regional Connectivity: Can unmapped race routes or adjacent lands be formalized into contiguous multi-use trail corridors?
  • Regional Network Expansion: Formalizing social trails and old race routes turns unmapped terrain into official, multi-use trail corridors.

 

Threats (External Risks)

What outside challenges could impede your goals?

  • Permitting & Bureaucracy: Are local environmental reviews or DNR approval processes stalling critical trail extension projects?
  • Transition Resistance: Will local legacy members push back against shifting membership management or updated dues models?
  • Ecosystem Wear: Is rising trail traffic outpacing your chapter's physical and financial capacity to maintain trail quality and prevent erosion?

Key Points:

  1. Pay Nothing. Give Everything. We are keeping the costs low and the expectations high.
  2. For ‘26 we’re keeping the same racy 55.5 mile distance but on an entirely  NEW ROUTE.
  3. Bringing back the Fixed category for those dumb enough to try.
  4. If you register and later decide not to participate, please edit your entry in BikeReg and move yourself to the category “I'm OUT - I can no longer participate.” Thanks in advance.
  5. Registration is open on BikeReg until a night or two before race day (and it's free) so no “day of” registration. Renegade if you want but no podium for you. We got stuff to do on race day and don't have time to bend our lives to your poor planning.

Schedule:

  • Saturday, October 3, 2025, Cumming, Iowa, at The Cumming Tap (117 N 44th St, Cumming, IA 50061)
  • 9a: check-in at The Cumming Tap and then gather yourself for the best singlespeed gravel race/ride of your life.
  • 9:45a: ease your way to the shiny brand new Cumming Main Street and then to the adjacent gravel Whatever Street for the start line and a few final minutes of self-doubt. Check your tires even though it's too late. Look for people who appear to know what they're doing and go to them.
  • 10a: Give Everything.
  • Sometime later…podiums and championship Wrangler flannel jerseys followed by pride and joy.

Rules (the written kind):

  1. You must be present to win.
  2. Bolt-on aero bars are not allowed.
  3. Yep, singlespeed bikes only.
  4. No outside support unless available to all racers. Racers may support other racers. And probably should.
  5. Each racer must have a pre-assigned friend/enemy to come pick them up in case of an issue. There is no transportation available from the race director. If you don’t show at the finish no one will come looking for you. YOU ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR YOU. 

Route

  1. Route (subject to change so never “save to my routes” until you know they are final):
    1. UPDATED 9/28/2026 DUE TO ROAD CONSTRUCTION…
      1. WET conditions (none B Roads) - 4100ft climb
  2. Course will not be marked and it is on open roads. You will be responsible for all routing and must abide by all traffic laws. We will have a crack staff of volunteers at the key spots. Don’t trust the RWGPS ascent estimates cuz they are always low by a gazillion percent (roughly 25%). Plan on 4K feet of climb and a route that's over 95% gravel.
  3. There is a convenience store on the Championship route in St Charles, and we'll have a couple spots to breathe life back into you with liquids and calories.
  4. There are no formal checkpoints, so you do NOT need to stop anywhere on the course - this is a race with championships on the line! Make sure to cross the various chipless timing mats out there for accurate splits for the real-time closed circuit satellite feed to The Cumming Tap. Wave to the hidden cameras.
  5. Some beautiful B road are on the route. They can be smooth, sketchy, mud, or a combination of all three, so be careful. If it's too wet, we will eliminate the B Roads entirely (see the WET and DRY route links to RideWithGPS.
  6. The route is hard and you’re dumb to do it. Do not attempt this race unless you have previously ridden a similar distance on singlespeed on hilly gravel and not died. Not kidding…it is hard.
  7. Tires & gravel conditions…the gravel roads on the route are LIMESTONE with a firm base so you don’t need big ‘ol tires unless you like how they roll. No sandy/pebble roads. The B roads are dirt and fast when dry - just gotta be careful of washouts/ruts. There will likely be fresh gravel here and there to dash your hopes and sidewalls.
  8. Chipless timing provided by Sundial Chrono.

Quitting:

  1. Call/text your pre-assigned friend/enemy to come get you because no one else will.
  2. Call/text Chris Kyhl so he also knows you’re OUT @ 515-554-7024.
  3. No one who does this race is a quitter. Unless you quit. Consider chasing the DFL Championship Jersey instead.

Podiums:

  1. Big budget podiums with trophies to write home about. Fastest person in each cat is the champ. That’s how bike races work.
  2. DFL Champ. Finish DFL without cutting course or getting a ride or any other sort of cheating and win a Wrangler champ jersey just like the winners which clearly indicates you were DFL. Wear around town amongst your gravel singlespeeding circle and impress those losers. You clearly worked harder than anyone else and deserve a DFL Champ jersey more than the overall winner. Mainly because they won and you were DFL.
  3. KOM. This was new in ‘25 and worked well. Probably do something similar in ‘26. Or, maybe we’ll do a Green Points Flannel with some intermediate sprints. You never know

The Pisgah 111 is the quintessential crusher of a cross-country endurance MTB race. Racers follow a 65.1 mile course with 10,200' feet of climbing along the most iconic trails and gravel roads known in Pisgah National Forest. Just peek at the course map and list of trails and you’ll immediately get chills just thinking about the epic scenery and terrain you’ll encounter.

There will be FOUR rest areas (at three locations) for the Pisgah 111  that will be stocked with water, food (PB&J, fruit, salty snacks, sweet snacks,  bars), first aid, and neutral mechanical support. Riders may send drop bags to each rest area. Be sure to read the information below, too. 

The Pisgah 555 will test the strength and endurance of racers by challenging them to complete a 39.7 mile course with 7325' of climbing and is nearly 100% Pisgah single-track. The course traverses some of the great Pisgah classics: Black Mountain, Turkey Pen Gap, Laurel Mountain, and Pilot Rock.

The Pisgah 555 is open to cyclists AND runners.
There will be THREE rest areas for the Pisgah 555 that will be stocked with water, food (PB&J, fruit, salty snacks, sweet snacks, bars), and first aid. Racers may send drop bags to each Rest Area.

Year 12~ Can You Beleive IT! ~Vermont Rare Gravel!

Happy to see have you back for another year!  You'll see some new, some old and somewhere in between.  Keeping it around 45miles this year….but we're turning up the climbing on a few new roads.  

Why not #vermontraregravelride this Year?

   


"Grassroots GRavel" at its Finest! 

It's not a Race, It's an Adventure!  

The Hidden Gem of Southern VT

What to Expect 

This is not a Race, However the front usually has Pace, But fast or slow LET'S obey the rules of the road = Don't be a Dick!  12th year running back to our original distance of 45 miles, 4500 vertical feet of climbing with 5 sections of good ole VT Class IV.  The most challenging could be the 19% up Johnson Hill Road.  40mm plus tires and gearing to keep your legs fresh are recommended.    

9:30 Start Time

  • Little Michigan to Stone Place

There are a few short sections that some riders may want to dismount and walk or jog.  And that's Okay, go  your own pace; the challenge is as important as the journey!  

*  As we did in 2020 We will be adhering to the Vermont State Covid guidelines if required.  https://accd.vermont.gov/covid-19/restart/cross-state-travel   Please mask if you are not vaccinated and keep your 6 feet of distance.   

 

Equipment Recommendation

This ride is calling for cross, gravel, flat bar mountain, or the like ~highly discourage any road bikes!  38 cc and above tire choice will serve you well.  There is no "hike-a-bike" ALL totally ridable Class IV.

Water + Food

There will be 2 refueling/ Feed stations; one at 14 miles (top of Marsh Cross and Dale Road) and 28 miles at the top of Holt Mtn Class IV stocked with GU gels, GU hydration, bananas, pickles, syrup shots and more. We do recommend you carry plenty of water and your own nutrition as well.

Plenty of parking at Wild Wings Nordic Center.  Follow Hapgood Road east out of Peru Center.  At the town garage bear left onto North Road.  Follow North Rd. appox. 2 miles, bear left at the folk, 500 meters to Wild Wings XC.

I started this endeavor twelve years ago as a passionate cyclist with a cause.  Building community, Advocating for a cause, challenged with the parallels between gravel riding/ racing, walking the rare disease journey and educating myself and others, about childhood rare disease.  I am not a charity but work directly with Vermont Rare, Rasopathies Network, CFC International amongst others to educate people on rare disease and finding ways to improve the lives of young people and families that live with a rare disease.  So if you to are passionate about something, enjoy strong community and friends, do things with a purpose, love to ride and are excited about a new challenge, Vermont Rare Gravel might be the perfect fit!

Cider Cross / Fon Solo Weekend 2026! 

Year Six — Bigger, Better, and More Fun Than Ever!
[October 3-4| Alna, ME]

Forget the pumpkin spice — we’ve got a sour batch of apples ready to be mashed!

Join us for a two-day festival of fall mayhem featuring short-track MTB & CX racing, last-person-standing style trail running, epic gravel rides, and camping under the stars. Whether you're racing, riding, running, or just hanging out by the fire, Cider Cross / Fon Solo has something for everyone.

SATURDAY: CIDER CROSS + BACKYARD ULTRA-STYLE RUN

Cider Cross Race:

  • One 40-minute race with CX and MTB categories
  • About a 1-mile course
  • Expect slop, speed, and heckling
  • Bring any bike — gravel, mountain, cyclocross — whatever rolls!
  • Yes, the optional fire jump is back.
  • Yes, there will be prizes (top 3 per category, TBD)

Last-Person-Standing Trail Run:

  • Race format an easier version of the Backyard Ultra
  • ~1 mile loops on the same course
  • Time limit decreases by 1 minute per lap
    (e.g., Lap 1 = 20 min, Lap 2 = 19 min, etc.)
  • Run till you can't make the cutoff!
  • You can expect 7–8 laps if you're at a 12-min/mile pace
  • Last year, the fastest runners made it down to the 6-minute mark!

Free access to charcoal grills and camping available.

BYOBreakfast! (But seriously, sign up for a camping spot early.)

SUNDAY: THE FON SOLO GRAVEL LOOP

Our grand finale — a gravel adventure through the Sheepscot Valley. This year, we’ve got three route options:

The Old Fashioned Gravel ride/race is back for 2026! We are fortunate enough to have some of the best gravel riding in the Midwest and have put together four routes to show off the local terrain. EventName: Gorey Hollows VIII: The Hollow Heart
EventNotes:
The Gorey Hollows features some of the SKOV (Southwest Kingdom of Vermont’s) most scenic (and gnar) ATB riding.  Plus ya know, Class 4 roads which are dirt roads that are not generally maintained and sorta left to fall to pieces. Poultney’s road maintenance budget is basically non-existent, so our class 4 roads are wonderfully terrible.  Expect wash outs, ‘gravel’ the size of GMO grapefruits, steep hike a bike grades and wonderful views. The ride weaves in and out of the woods and farm lands.  Plenty of climbing but lots of great eye candy, like cows and red barns.  

4 ride options for ‘26.  There's the classic brutal 90 mile ATB race, with the rocky class 4 roads and extended hike a bikes, the 60 mile Scramble (pick any two of the ATB race loops) and the Ramble (pick any 1 of the ATB race loops). We also have added in an ‘Amble’ ride, for folks who wanna get out and enjoy the changing seasons but don't want to walk up some terrible climb or do huge miles.  Finally, we're making the ‘Just hanging out’ option permanent.  If you or your friend / partner / etc wants to just come, drink some good coffee, eat a donut, and chow down on some dinner, this is the category for you.  More info on the ride options at the bottom of these notes. 
 

All Routes are self navigated with minimal or no sag.  You'll get a GPS track and some notes, that's it.  No sag, no medical support, nothing but a nice camp fire to come back to and some good food.  

All Analog events are rain or shine.  If you think you can't make it, get the event insurance, it's only a few bucks.  No refunds for cancelations.  It's like a concert, not a dinner reservation.   

If you are racing, your race fee gets you dinner, but not breakfast, cause no one is eating anything at 4am.  If you are doing any of the other categories, your entry fee gets you a pour over coffee, a handmade donut, and a big autumnal dinner spread from our friends at the Poultney Pub.

A note about camping: in the past, we've had folks sign up for camping thru bikereg.  This year, we're doing the camping registration thru hip camp.  It'll cost you less if you're in a group or even if there is just two of you.  We'll email info about camping sign ups to you as soon as you register.  

In the spirit of Choose Your Own Adventure books (originally published in Vermont!) you decide your destiny.  Three possible loops.  Racers have to do all 3, but pick the order of the loops.  Scramblers pick any 2 and choose the order.  Ramblers pick one.  Loops start and end at the sugar house HQ, so you can restock on water, food, clothing. 

The Amble is 15ish miles. Dirt roads, a rail trail, a class 4 road, one big hill. It's doable, chill, you can use any bike that isn't a road bike, more or less. Ideally 38mm plus tires and low gearing. James will be leading this ride, very slow group pace.

The Ramble is 30ish miles, dirt roads, plenty of climbing, bushwacking, singletrack and some sketchy class 4 roads.  Doable on a bike with decently low gearing and 50mm tires.  One of the loops has less than 4k of climbing, most ramblers will probably want to do that.  This is a very hard 30 miles. It took ramblers over 5 hours last year. Self Navigated.

The Scramble is 60ish miles.  Very difficult, even if you pick the easiest loop and one of the two hard loops.  Many riders will not finish the scramble.  You need to bring lights in case you get caught in the dark.  Lots of folks will not finish the 60 miles before sundown.  Self Navigated.

The Race is 90ish miles, with around 13,000 feet of climbing.  Singletrack, horrible rocky roads, check points, hike a bikes, and other sketch delights.  Hardest, most ridiculous ATB ride you'll ever do, we bet.  1 rider finished the race last year, out of a field of 25 or so.  Starts early.  Totally self supported old school race.   Winner gets a nice alloy ATB wheelset, second place gets pie and third some donuts.  You have to do all 3 loops to win, in any order.  Loops are directional. You can pick which to start with but you have to do them in a set direction. Self Navigated.

Rules for 2026 race: 

  • To podium, the following stuff is banned:  Aero Bars, Suspension forks, suspension frames, suspension Seatposts and stems.  E bikes are of course banned.  You can race with any of this stuff, but your results will not count toward the official record.
  • Mandatory Race time cuts so we are not up till 11pm waiting for you to come back.
  • One bike, one set of wheels and tires.  No swapping bikes like it’s a cross race.
  • Racers can refuel, change clothes, take naps, at Analog HQ in between loops.
  • Mandatory check in after every loop.  

The Gorey Hollows is a different kinda ride.  No ride leader.  No sag wagon.  It's more like a free for all with a common course and goal.    These roads are impassable to all but the most modified jeeps.  Nothing is marked.  You have to use your cue sheet and a GPS track to make it through.That's not impossible, but you have to pay attention.  There won't be any cell service for most of the ride. We will release the GPX track a few days before the race via email. 

Pre Ride Stuff: 

Racers: get here at 4:00, race starts at 5am.  Scramblers:  Leave at 8am.  Ramblers: Leave at 10am.  Amblers leave at 11am. Donuts and coffee at 7:30am and 9am

Equipment requirements for 30, 60 and 90 mile ride:

  • Sturdy walking shoes
  • Low enough gearing to make it up 15% grades that are loose and wet
  • Spare tubes/tubeless patch kits
  • Tire boots
  • GPS or Phone with GPS ability with some sort of back up battery situation.
  • Ride with GPS or GAIA.
  • 1.75" / 44mm wide tires or bigger.  Advise 2.25 or bigger.  Most past winners rode 2.8” tires.
  • Basic tools and bike repair know-how in case you break down
  • First Aid stuff.
  • There are no sag wagons!  There is no way to get out of the woods!  Be safe.  Ride Smart.

Post ride:  

Fire pit hangs at the old Analog Sugar House.  Cheer on racers as they finish laps and become more and more worn out! Autumn Feast provided by our friends at Poultney Pub.  If you saw the taco scene at the 4x4 you know these will be good.  Optional camping at the Analog HQ as well.  We’ll have some refreshments, but mainly this is a BYOB kinda deal.

The Tucker Tour is what you get when you connect all of the amazing Class VI roads in and around Mount Kearsarge and Ragged Mountain in beautiful central New Hampshire. What is a Class VI road you ask? Well, the state of NH defines a Class VI road as an existing public way that has “not been maintained and repaired by the town in suitable condition for travel thereon for 5 successive years or more.”

What does this mean for those of you looking to tackle the Tucker Tour? Well, you can expect every sort of terrain, from paved and gravel roads all the way to completely unrideable hike-a-bike paths through the woods and everything in between. The 80 mile course has only 15 miles of paved roads and around 38 miles of unmaintained Class VI. Many of these paths are quite steep, which only adds to the difficulty. In summary, this is a ride that is much harder than its distance might indicate.

 

If the 80 mile course seems a bit much, there is a 62, 36, and a 24 mile course as well.  We strongly suggest loading multiple routes on to your computer/phone in case you start on the 62 mile route, but don’t have great legs and need to switch to the 36 mile route.

 

This is a 100% self-supported ride. Each participant is expected to be able to navigate on their own using the provided .gpx route or Strava route. There is no cue sheet and no navigational aids along the course. As far as provisions go, there are 2 general stores/gas stations along the route at approximately 19 miles and 54 miles.

So, what do you get for participating?  Besides the satisfaction of completing something that is incredibly hard, each participant will receive a sticker and a mug featuring this year’s unique logo design!

 

We will also be hosting a casual post-ride get together starting at 5:00 pm.  Pizza and beverages will be served, however, if you want to bring a post ride treat to share with your fellow participants, you are more than welcome to do so!

You can find more information, including a FAQ section, at lioncreekdesign.com/tucker-tour-26.

A big shout out to Josh and the Class VI Classic for showing the way.  So much of this ride is inspired by what he has put on up in Etna, NH.  If you think you would enjoy the Tucker Tour, you would have a great time in June at the Class VI Classic.

*** Registration is now Closed. We are at our maximum number of riders.  There will be NO Onsite Registration. ***

PLEASE NOTE THE FOLLOWING IMPORTANT INFORMATION:

  • Minors:  Girls 3 to 17 years of age when riding with an adult are FREE, limit of 40 free entries.  Girls ages 3 to 7 must ride with an adult parent or guardian on a tandem bike in a child's seat, in a child's seat on a tagalong bike, or in a bike trailer.  Girls ages 8 to 17 may ride on their own pedal bike.  Girls ages 8 to 13 must ride with an adult parent or guardian.
  • Recommended Start Times:  This is not a race.  We recommend starting the 56 mile ride at 7:30 am, the 34 mile ride at 8:30 am, and the Family ride at 10 am.
  • Potential Food Allergies:  Prepackaged gluten-free options will be available at the rest stops. Gluten-free options will also be available at lunch but cross-contamination cannot be guaranteed.
  • Automated Emails. Be sure to enter a valid email address that you check regularly since that is where you will get updates and important information about the ride.
  • Multiple Registrants. You can register more than one rider during your session, however each rider must individually sign the liability waiver. Keep in mind if you are riding tandem that both the Captain and Stoker must register. ALL fields marked with a * are required.
  • Editing and Transferring Registrations. If you would like the ability to view, edit, or transfer your registration after purchase, it’s best to use the FREE “Join Outside+” option when checking out. Transferring registrations is done completely online at BikeReg.com (other than finding someone to transfer to and payment arrangements)
  • No Refunds. You can Transfer your registration to someone else if you cannot attend. Transferring a paid entry simply requires that you log into your BikeReg account and choose the “Transfer” option.  Follow the directions to complete a transfer to another person who has paid you directly for the entry.
  • SRCC Event Cancellation Policy. SRCC reserves the right to cancel or reschedule an event when, in SRCC’s sole discretion, it is reasonably necessary to do so. Circumstances under which cancellation or rescheduling may occur include, but are not limited to, Acts of God, terrorism, community disasters, such as earthquake, fire or flooding, or other unforeseen events reasonably likely to compromise the safety of participants or otherwise interfere with the ability of the club to hold the event. Inclement weather alone will generally not result in a cancellation. Events are held rain or shine. If the event is cancelled:

1. Participants will be notified as soon as possible.

2. Depending on the situation, full or partial refunds may be issued in SRCC’s sole discretion.

 

SRCC relies on fees from our events to continue our stated purpose as a 501(c)(4) non-profit recreational cycling club to ensure our organization is here every year, to continue advocating for riders and putting on the best events in the country. SRCC must honor commitments and contracts many of which are paid in advance of the event and non-refundable. SRCC cannot bear the risk of a disaster alone. Each participant accepts the risk of losing his or her registration fee or other incidental expenses related to participation in the event should circumstances warranting cancellation arise. Thanks for your support and understanding.

EventNotes:
Buffalo River Gran Fondo – October 3, 2026

Start/Finish: Second Stage, Amherst, VA

The Buffalo River Gran Fondo returns in 2026 to Second Stage in the heart of Amherst, VA. After a beautiful ride through some of the finest gravel in the George Washington National Forest, you’ll roll back into town for food, music, and community—just like we started. We’re stoked to celebrate where it all began.

Ride Options

  • The BIG Buffalo: 108 miles | 13k' elevation gain | 65% gravel, 35% pavement 

Designed for the not-so-smart who enjoy suffering more than most. GPS Route: Strava

  • The Full Monty: 68 miles | ~7,000' elevation gain | ~65% gravel, 35% pavement
    Take on the classic Alhambra Road climb and four Strava KOM/QOM segments. Recommended for gravel bikes or endurance road bikes with 32c tires or wider.     GPS Routes: Strava | RidewithGPS | Garmin

  • Lil’ Shorty: 32.2 miles | ~2,600' elevation gain | ~20% gravel, 80% pavement
    Designed for our road bike friends and the gravel-curious. 32c tires are ideal; experienced riders may be fine on 28c. Features two Strava segments.   GPS Routes: Strava | RidewithGPS | Garmin

     

Strava Segment Challenge

Compete for the coveted Buffalo Skull by logging the lowest combined time across your route’s Strava segments.


Join our Strava club and make sure you record your ride to be eligible. More info here

 

Weekend Schedule

Friday, October 2

  • Afternoon check-in at Loose Shoe Brewery
  • Beer and pzza  (available for purchase)
  • Complimentary camping for riders and families at the Amherst County Admin Building

Saturday, October 3

  • 8:00 AM: Coffee, light breakfast, and rider briefing
  • 9:30 AM: Both routes depart
  • Post-ride meal, beer ticket, and commemorative swag
  • Extra food and drinks are available for friends and family

Camping & Lodging

  • On-site Camping: Primitive camping is available at Camp Trapezium, with access to a portable shower
  • Lodging Nearby:
    • Sweet Briar College's Elston Inn (Amherst, VA)
    • Hotels and inns in Lynchburg, VA

Support & Amenities

  • Well-marked courses with downloadable GPS files
  • Three rest stops on the Full Monty; two on Lil’ Shorty
  • SAG vehicle and on-course support
  • Great post-ride atmosphere with food, drink, and good people

Location

Second Stage
194 Second Street, Amherst, VA 24521

More info: mmgendurancesports.com/buffalo-river-gran-fondo

EventNotes:
ROUTES: Hyperlink for both routes will be provided when available on both RideWithGPS and Garmin Connect platform.

 

CUSTOM EVENT JERSEY 

Stay tuned for details to purchase custom ride jersey.

 

RIDE vs. RACE  and PRIZES

Please remember this is a ride for a great cause and not a race for a trophy. We plan to ride together in small groups, which is safer and more fun. Since the event is not timed we've decided to award prizes using a raffle approach. Riders will receive a raffle ticket with their packet at the end. After the ride at our celebration event, we will draw tickets for door prizes donated by our sponsors.

 

RIDE CATEGORIES

There are only two categories for this year's event, a Full-Pull and a Fun-Ride. For the longer Full-Pull, riders will start together at Backlick Road Station and riders for the short Fun-Ride will start together at a later time at Manassas Park Station (as the peloton passes through).
 
DEPARTURE AND RETURN:

Full-Pull riders may choose to begin their day at either Manassas (Broad Run Station) or Springfield (Backlick Road Station). 

If you start in Manassas at Broad Run Station, transportation will be provided to the starting line.  You may park at the Broad Run Station. Please know that the transportation will depart at 8:00 a.m. with or without you, so don't be late!

If you choose to begin in Springfield at Backlick Road Station, please park at the station and plan to join the pre-ride briefing at 8:45 a.m.

The ride departs Backlick Road Station promptly at 9:00 a.m.

Transportation will return riders to the starting point. The transportation will depart Broad Run Station promptly at 1:30 p.m. If you need a ride back, don't miss it!

 

RIDE ESCORT and GEAR STORAGE and SUPPORT

For the safety of the group we have arranged for escort vehicles within and at the rear of the peloton. Riders will be able to store their gear (such as a jacket you may shed as we ride) in one of the vehicles and retrieve items at the end. Additionally, if a rider has a mechanical/flat, they can place their bike in a vehicle and ride to the next station stop for support.

 

HOTEL ACCOMODATIONS

If you don't want an early start, consider staying overnight. We have not reserved a block of rooms but there are rooms available in nearby Manassas on the south end of the route and nearby Springfield on the north end of the route. 

 

BREAST CANCER AWARENESS and PINK SOCKS

October is Breast Cancer Awareness Month. This ride is meant to raise awareness, especially for Triple-Negative Breast Cancer. Some of us ride in memory of our friend Maria Foster.  We'll be adding a link below to the JustGiving.com website.  We ask that you wear PINK socks for the ride.

The countdown is on! Here’s everything you need to know to make sure you're ready for this year's AFO 100.

 

Event Details

 

DATE: Saturday, October 3

TIME: Registration opens at 6:30 A.M. | Ride begins at 8:00 A.M.

LOCATION: Cumming City Center, 423 Canton Road, Cumming

PARKING: Primary parking is in the new lot by Crooked Culture (see below). If that lot is full, additional parking is available near the Courthouse/Police building. It’s just a short walk to Registration at building 421, Crooked Culture Brewing.

 

Download Your Route 

Whether you're aiming for 40 miles, 62 miles, or going all out for the 100 miles, you’ll want to stay on track every step of the way. Be sure to download the detailed, turn-by-turn routes straight to your bike computer for extra confidence. The course will be marked with AFO arrows, but having the maps makes it easier to anticipate what’s ahead. You’ll also find the scheduled rest stops marked along each route.

 

Ride Groups 

This year’s ride will feature six pace groups, giving every cyclist the opportunity to find a group that feels like the right fit. On event day, simply look for the sign marking your pace group and connect with the ride leaders. The first group will roll out at 8:00 A.M., with a short interval between each group that follows to help keep everyone moving comfortably.

 

 

For those not riding in a group, you’re free to ride at any pace that is comfortable for you. We encourage you to connect with others riding at a similar speed. It’s a great way to share the miles, support each other, and make the whole experience even more fun.

 

Saturday Morning Schedule

6:00 A.M. – Volunteers arrive at Crooked Culture Brewing

6:30 A.M. – Registration/late packet pickup at Crooked Culture Brewing

7:15 A.M. – All cyclists should be on-site

7:30 A.M. – Cyclist staging by pace group begins

7:45 A.M. – All cyclists should be in their corral and ready to ride

8:00 A.M. – Ride start

11:00 A.M. – Lunch and beer service begins 

1:30 P.M. – Post-ride celebration at Crooked Culture Brewing

2:00 P.M. – Raffle at Crooked Culture Brewing

4:00 P.M. – Support services end

 

Reminders

Cumming City Center restrooms will be open at 6:00 A.M. In addition, portable restrooms will be located in both the primary parking lot and the remote parking lot.

 

You will receive a meal ticket and a drink ticket at packet pickup. Your meal ticket is good for up to $15 at one of these participating Cumming City Center restaurants: HomeStead, SliceAbility, Los Rios Cantina, Rise & Slice Deli & Bakery, Dominic’s Wood Fired, The Well, or Washington's Wharf. Treat yourself to whatever looks good! 


Use your drink ticket to grab a refreshing soft drink or a celebratory beer at any of the same restaurants, as well as at Crooked Culture Brewery. The choice is yours!

 

Capture those moments and share them! Be sure to post your photos to social media and tag us using #AFO2026.

AFO Raffle

The AFO Raffle is back with another lineup of prizes you won’t want to miss!

Along with cycling gear, apparel, and other fun prizes, one lucky winner will take home an incredible:

4-DAY / 3-NIGHT STAY AT AN OCEANFRONT BEACH CONDO IN PANAMA CITY BEACH, FLORIDA!

Ready to try your luck? Grab your tickets before the ride and you could be on your way to an unforgettable beach getaway!

 

Safety First

We’ve got your back! Our safety team will be onsite throughout the event, and help is just a call away. Save and use the LIVE support line, (470) 238-9465, if you need any help during the ride.

Inclement Weather
We’ll be monitoring the weather closely throughout the week. If inclement weather requires any changes to the event schedule, we’ll notify all registered participants by email and post updates on our Facebook page. Please keep an eye out for updates as we get closer to Saturday.
 

Riding with Purpose

As we gather for this year’s ride, we’ll also take a moment to remember Van and the love, grace, and kindness he shared so generously with our cycling community. His influence is still felt in the people and friendships that make this group so special, and we’re grateful to continue honoring his memory as we celebrate the 8th anniversary of the ALL FOR ONE ride. More than just a day on the bike, this ride is a chance to challenge ourselves, enjoy the miles, and celebrate the community we’ve built together.

We can’t wait to ride together and make this year’s ALL FOR ONE another great day.

See you at the starting line!

Registration

 

The AFO 100 is back and better than ever, kicking off at 8:00 a.m. sharp on Saturday, October 3, 2026, from Cumming City Center in Cumming, Georgia. Prepare to be blown away as you embark on a thrilling journey through picturesque landscapes and challenging terrain. But that's just the beginning of the excitement.
 

Choose Your Challenge

This year’s routes are designed to thrill, with pristine roads, scenic landscapes, and unforgettable views. Riders can choose from three distances:

  • 40 miles with 2,800 feet of elevation (AFO Fondo 40)
  • 62 miles with 4,400 feet of elevation (AFO Gran Fondo, AFO Express, AFO Club Ride)
  • 100 miles with 6,800 feet of elevation (AFO Century Express, Knight Ride, AFO Club Ride)

All routes wind through the charming countryside and feature some of the best rolling terrain in the region. Navigate the course with ease using turn-by-turn routes (40, 62, 100) for your bike computer, ensuring you stay ahead of the pack!
 

AFO Club Full Century, Presented by Wahoo

Looking for the ultimate way to tackle 100 miles with confidence, camaraderie, and expert support? The AFO Club full century is built for cyclists who want to go big, ride strong, and enjoy every mile along the way. Limited to just 30 cyclists, this exclusive weekend experience combines premium ride support and unique access to two of cycling’s most recognizable personalities.

Not sure you’re ready for the full century? No problem. At mile 48, you’ll have the option to continue on for the full 100 miles or finish with the 62-mile group instead. Either way, you’ll be part of an unforgettable ride experience that’s both challenging and rewarding.

This fully supported experience includes:

  • Exclusive AFO Club access limited to just 30 cyclists
  • Friday night social and shakeout ride with Wahoo professional World Tour athletes Ian Boswell (@ian_boswell) • Instagram photos and videos and Alison M. Tetrick (@amtetrick) • Instagram photos and videos
  • Leadership and pacing during Saturday’s AFO from Ian, Alison, and experienced Domestique Riders
  • Full moto support throughout the ride
  • A Wahoo Support Van stocked with hydration, snacks, and tools for minor mechanical issues
  • An average pace of 18–19 mph, ideal for riders looking for a strong, supported century experience

More than just a ride, the AFO Club is a shared experience built around challenge, encouragement, and the joy of riding together. If you’re looking for an unforgettable century with incredible support and community, this is your ride.
 

The Knight Ride

Once again, this year’s ride features special guest Andrew Knight, a 12-time U.S. National Champion and the 2025 World Time Trial Champion. Riders can join him on the exclusive Knight Ride, an adrenaline-packed 100-mile experience where you’ll test your limits and ride shoulder-to-shoulder with a national champ.


Designed for advanced cyclists seeking a truly elite ride experience, this century includes: 

  • Leadership and pacing from Andrew Knight and experienced Domestique Riders
  • Full moto support throughout the ride
  • An average pace of 22 mph for riders seeking a serious challenge

It’s a rare opportunity to learn from one of the best, push your pace, and elevate your ride like never before. If you're looking for speed, strategy, and a next-level cycling experience, this is where you want to be.

 

AFO Century Express

Ready to take on 100 miles at a faster pace with elite-level support behind you? The AFO Century Express is built for strong, experienced riders looking for a smooth, high-performance century experience. This group ride is ideal for cyclists ready to push the pace while still benefiting from an organized and fully supported team environment.


This supported century includes: 

  • Leadership and pacing from experienced Domestique Riders
  • Full moto support throughout the ride
  • An average pace of 19 mph for riders looking to keep the tempo high

The Century Express delivers the perfect balance of speed, teamwork, and support, helping riders stay efficient, connected, and confident from the first mile to the finish line.

 

 

AFO Express


Ready to take on 62 miles at a strong pace with elite-level support behind you? The AFO Express is built for experienced riders looking to keep the tempo high while enjoying a smooth, fully supported ride experience. This group ride is ideal for cyclists who want to challenge themselves, ride efficiently, and stay connected with a strong team from start to finish.

This supported ride includes:

  • Leadership and pacing from experienced Domestique Riders
  • Full moto support throughout the ride
  • An average pace of 19 mph for riders looking to maintain a strong tempo

With a steady pace, experienced riders around you, and support every mile of the way, the AFO Express is designed to keep you moving strong and make every mile count.

 

AFO Gran Fondo

Ready to take on 62 miles with a strong group and plenty of support along the way? The Gran Fondo is designed for experienced cyclists who want to challenge themselves while enjoying the camaraderie and energy of a well-supported group ride. It’s a great option for riders looking to ride strong, stay together, and enjoy the journey.

This supported ride includes:

  • Leadership and pacing from experienced Domestique Riders
  • Full moto support throughout the ride
  • An average pace of 17 mph for riders looking to maintain a steady, challenging tempo

The Gran Fondo brings together great miles, a strong pace, and an experienced team to create a rewarding ride from start to finish.

 

AFO Fondo 40

Ready to ride 40 miles with a great group and support along the way? The AFO Fondo 40 is a welcoming option for cyclists who want to challenge themselves, enjoy the ride, and experience the camaraderie of a fully supported group. This ride gives you the freedom to settle into a comfortable rhythm while still enjoying the energy of the group.

This supported ride includes:

  • Leadership and pacing from experienced Domestique Riders
  • Full moto support throughout the ride
  • A 12–15 mph pace range designed to keep the group together

The AFO Fondo 40 is all about enjoying the miles, riding with good people, and crossing the finish line feeling strong.

Refuel and Recharge at Fully Supported Rest Stops

Take a well-deserved break and replenish your energy at our fully stocked rest stops along the route. With refreshing drinks and nourishing nutrition options, you'll power through those challenging miles with renewed vigor. Scheduled rest stops are as follows:

  • Mile 23 - Mt. Vernon Church (Kelly Bridge)
  • Mile 45 - Mt. Pisgah Baptist Church (Pisgah)
  • Mile 61 - Valero Gas (Union Hill)
  • Mile 71 - Valero Gas (Union Hill)
  • Mile 89 - Mt. Pisgah Baptist Church (Pisgah)
     

Perks That Make the Ride Even Sweeter

Your ride comes with more than just a great route. Every registered rider will receive:

  • A super soft, commemorative, long-sleeve AFO 100 t-shirt
  • A celebratory beer at Crooked Culture Brewery
  • A post-ride lunch from one of Cumming City Center’s local eateries
  • Free downloadable event photos
  • One free prize giveaway ticket
     

Incredible Prizes

This year’s AFO prize giveaway is loaded with cool cycling gear, gift cards, and other awesome prizes from our sponsors.

Prize giveaway tickets are $20 each, and 100% of proceeds support the Van Purser Foundation. It’s a fun, easy way to give back, and maybe even go home with some great stuff. You also have the opportunity to make a direct donation to the Van Purser Foundation, making a meaningful difference in the lives of cyclists and their families during challenging times.

So, what are you waiting for? Strap on your helmet, clip in, and join us for an unforgettable cycling experience at the 2026 AFO 100.

EventName: The 2026 Sloan Everett Pure Country Pedal Memorial Bike Ride
EventNotes:
Join us for the 10th Annual Sloan Everett Pure Country Pedal Memorial Bike Ride on Saturday, October 3, 2026, in Breckenridge, Texas. There's a route for everyone, whether you're chasing a serious distance or bringing the whole family out for the day.

Five routes roll through the ranch land and rolling hills of Stephens County: the Greenhorn (4.22 miles), the Pony Express (7.79 miles), the Buckin' Bronc (18.73 miles), the Top Hand (31.62 miles), and Sloan's Route (59.07 miles). Every turn is marked, and ride support is strong. We keep this event small on purpose, so you'll never get lost in the shuffle or on the road.

Adult registration is $45 and includes an event t-shirt and a BBQ lunch ticket. Youth 13-17 yrs are $30, and kids 12 and under ride free! Pre-registered riders are guaranteed their t-shirt size, so sign up early to lock yours in.

The day starts and ends at Breckenridge City Park. After the ride, stick around for a hearty BBQ lunch, live music from Max & Heather Stalling, a kids' play area and bounce house, and the kind of hometown welcome you only find in a small Texas town. The last rider in eats as well as the first and gets cheered the loudest. That's a promise.

Here's what makes this ride different: 100% of net proceeds go straight to our local volunteer fire departments, the Caddo, Hubbard Creek, and Wayland VFDs. We ride to honor Sloan Everett, a true pure country hero who gave his life protecting his family's cattle from a wildfire in 2017, and we ride to support the firefighters who answer the call every day.

Come ride with purpose. Saddle up, and we'll see you in October!

EventNotes:
Silver Creek Sprint Enduro @ Silver Creek Bike Park, Berea Kentucky

 

Welcome to the 

Silver Creek Sprint Enduro!

Whether you are a seasoned racer or new to enduro, we invite you to enjoy this fun and exciting race. We will be offering multiple race options with both male and female categories in Pro, Expert, Beginner, and Junior, with two mixed gender categories in Hardtail and E bike. *Costumes encouraged

What is a sprint enduro mountain bike race?

  • Riders are timed only on the downhill stages.
  • The transfer climbs between stages are usually shorter than in a full enduro.
  • There are often fewer stages as well.
  • The entire event can often be completed in a few hours rather than taking most of a day.
  • Courses tend to emphasize speed, flow, and quick transitions while still including technical features.

 

How will the timing of stages work?

With entry fees being set the lowest in the land and covering both race operations and post-race meals, timing will be conducted using a two-stopwatch manual timing system. This creates a little extra backend work us, but for you we guarantee reliable & accurate times. Racers will be stopped at the top of every stage by a trail marshal and given a radio command when to start from the bottom of each stage. This will ensure that both stopwatches are started at the exact moment that each racer is given the command to begin the stage. As this being Silver Creek Bike Parks first enduro, making it affordable for everyone to participate is as important as getting accurate times. Although we are intending this to be a fun event for our community, we will be taking the racing serious and ensuring that we give you the most accurate times possible with a well-trained staff of timers and trail marshals.

EventName: Ann Arbor Short Track Mountain Bike Race
EventNotes:
Come enjoy a fun Saturday fall afternoon & evening racing mountain bikes on Ann Arbor's local loop 
Short track is a low-cost, low-key, high-fun mountain bike race for kids, teens and adults of all abilities! Races are 30 minutes or less and the course is not super technical. No experience with mountain biking necessary. 
$20 for adults • $15 for juniors  • FREE kids fun race • Spectators and cheer squad welcome
Location: Olson Park, 1515 Dhu Varren Rd in Ann Arbor. Olson trails are novice and intermediate friendly and are the northern portion of the Ann Arbor local mountain biking loop. 
Parking: In Olson Park 
Registration/Check-in: 
If you sign up for more than one race, the next race is only $5. 
Pre-registration on BikeReg is open until  15 min before each races race start time.  There is no in-person, cash late registration, it is online only! 
If you register on the same day of the race (anytime Saturday 10/3)  you must show electronic proof of registration/receipt when you check in to the race to receive a race bib. We ask this because race start sheets will have already been printed and you will not be on the list.
You must check in to get your race number. Please do this as soon as you get there so you have plenty of time to get ready for your race.  
Helmets: required at all times!
Start times: Start times are posted by the category you registered for. The fun begins at 3:30 with the best race - the kids fun race (9 and under), so come hang out in the park before your race! 
Course Notes: ~1 mile loop mostly on single track trail. There will be grassy and paved sections to allow for safe passing opportunities. Kids fun race is a 0.4 mile loop on paved, flat single track, and grass.  
How does STXC work?
The most laps you can do in given time for your category wins the race!  
How do I safely pass someone in my race?
When passing on the race course, do so respectfully and only when it is possible to do so safely and without contact with another rider. Actions that compromise the safety of other athletes will not be tolerated. There will be many sections of the course where it is wide open on grass or pavement and you can safely pass. 
Call out when passing slower racers. "Passing left" indicates you will be passing on their left, "passing on your right" indicates you will be passing on their right. It is the responsibility of passing riders to overtake safely. Riders should voice the command "passing" when overtaking another rider. Riders being passed must move over as quickly, efficiently, and as safely as possible. 
Racers riding a bicycle have the right of way over racers pushing a bicycle. When practical, racers pushing shall stay on the least rideable portion of the trail when being passed.  Lapped athletes must yield to overtaking athletes (taken from the MiSCA-Racing-Rules-2026)
What type of bikes are allowed?
  • no E-Bikes are allowed. Every bike must have brakes.
  • Kids racer and Beginner Category racer are allowed to ride any type of non-electronic bike (mountain bike, cruiser, gravel bike)
  • Juniors, Intermediate and Advanced categories must race a flat bar, mountain bike. 
Will there be awards?
We will have podiums and prizes for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd in each category. There will be no cash prizes. You will get glory and bragging rights. All kids and juniors get a donut! 
Will there be food and drink?
We will have food available. Feel free to bring your own food, snacks, and drinks. 
When can I pre-ride the course?
Anytime! Olson park is open for mountain biking riding. If you want to ride the course when its taped off it will be open for pre-rides 10/3 1:30 to 3:30.

  • 36 mile ride with options to join or leave the ride at any point

  • Average speed 16-20mph. 2000 feet of climbing with rolling hills

  • Route will be on open roads in the New Paltz, Milton and Malboro area

  • The Ride with GPS route is HERE

  • Meeting location, parking, start and finish point is Twin Star Orchards

  • 8:50am Welcome remarks 

  • 9:00am sharp ride begins behind the White Bronco lead out vehicle

    • Police assistance possible at a few major road crossings

  • We will visit these farms in this order:

    • Twin Star Orchards

    • Minard’s Farm

    • Weed Orchard 

    • Locust Grove  

    • Dubois Farm

    • Twin Star Orchard afterparty

      • Donuts, Cider, Pizza, Burgers, Music

    • Delicious Donut Award point system to rate the donuts

       

  • Registration is $50 per rider

    • Includes a ticket for a donut or apple at each farm

    • CDBT water bottle

    • One cider drink at the finish

    • 10 minute recovery Normatec boot session

  • If registering for multiple riders, please register separately 

  • Additional donut tasting/food purchasing fees at each farm are covered by each rider on site 

    • Food at Twin Star Orchard afterparty is not included in registration

      We will aim to stay together as a group, stopping for 20 - 30 minutes at each farm and on to the next one

      Hand the ticket to the counter, receive donut or apple, taste, enjoy… and onward.  

  • Please ride with due regard for your surroundings, other cyclists and vehicles on the roadway

  • Ride safely and obey all traffic laws. Helmets are advised. Ride single file and to the right

  • Road or gravel bikes are recommended. Some gravel roads to farm entrances

  • Riders of all levels are welcome but this is a bit more moderate to advanced rider level with hills

  • No dogs please. Families and pups can meet at Twin Star for the afterparty

  • Ride is self supported regarding bike maintenance, flat tires and nutrition

    • We will have a water cooler for refills at farm stops

  • Ride is rain or shine

    • We will ride if it is raining light

    • Moderate to heavy continuous rain will cancel the ride

      • Registration fees could be carried over to new rescheduled date if it is postponed 

  • We are looking forward to another fun ride with you all!

  • Enjoy the beautiful views, pretty fall colors and social outdoor experience!

The Venue & Event

Druid Hill Park is a beautiful, historic 745 acre urban park established in 1859. In 2026 Charm City Cross will mark the 22nd annual race and our 11th year as a UCI sanctioned race. This is a two day Category 1 and 2 UCI and USA Cycling cyclocross event. The event will be held under UCI regulations and USA Cycling Permit # 15999. UCI scale of penalties and USAC penalties will apply.

COURSE DESCRIPTION

This is a traditional Charm City Cross course looping through the historic DRUID HILL PARK Baltimore Zoo Mansion House Lawn.  A Combination of pavement, grass, dirt and obstacles will be experienced. Course is roughly 1.8 miles

Course Map

Course Inspection and Warm-up

The course will be open for inspection and warm-up approximately 10 minutes prior to each event.  The officials will make an announcement when the course has been opened for inspection.  Warming up on the course during an event is strictly prohibited and will not be tolerated. Violations can result in disqualification. We suggest you inspect the course at least two slots before your race as you will need to get to the starting grid 15 minutes before your start time for staging.

There will be a UCI only course warm up period at 12:10 to 12:30. this is UCI ONLY.

IMPORTANT UCI START INFORMATION

Uci Elite riders please note the following:  

Start Line Protocol

Racers must report to the holding pen adjacent to the starting grid for staging 15 minutes before the start of their race. If you arrive late you will be staged at the next available position. 

Call-Up Protocol

Staging Procedure Riders shall be staged by the rider's assigned bib number.  Walk-up riders will be assigned remaining bib numbers on a first-come, first-served basis.  All riders will line up in the order of their numbers, filling gaps as allowed by the officials/callers.  Staging will fill the start grid as specified in the USAC rulebook start grid.

Staging Order for amateur races will be based on the most recent CrossResults.com ranking and USCX standings, using the following criteria:

The top 8 riders in the current USCX series standings who are pre-registered will be staged on the front row.

Remaining riders will be staged by CrossResults.com ranking.

All categories will reserve four spots in the third row, which are to be used for promoters’ discretion call-ups.

The first race of each year shall stage racers by their CrossResults.com ranking.

Those classes consisting of only cat 4/5 men or cat 4/5 women are staged by order of registration - starting with those who registered earliest.

UCI races will be called up per UCI regulations.

Feeding: 

For UCI races only:  No feeding is permitted. Riders are advised to add a water bottle on their bikes if necessary. Accepting hand-ups from spectators – including bottles, cans or money – is not permitted and will result in disqualification. No alcohol is permitted on the course or in the technical area.

For USAC races only: Rule 4A15: Feeding is generally not permitted unless specifically authorized by the Chief Referee. If authorized, there is normally no feeding in the first two and final two laps of the race. The location of feeding will be determined by the Chief Referee in conjunction with the Race Organization

Lapped Riders in UCI Events (UCI Rule 5.1.051): All riders lapped before the final lap must leave the race the next time they cross the finish line. The rider will be given a placing if he or she was lapped more than half way through the race.  A rider who is lapped on the final lap shall be stopped at the beginning of the finishing straight line and shall be given a placing on the basis of his or her position. Additionally, Commissaires may pull riders who are behind by more than 80% of the leader's lap time. 

Lapped Riders in Non-UCI Events: Lapped riders will finish on the same lap as the leaders. Riders in danger of being lapped must yield to oncoming racers and are not to interfere with their progress or trail behind them. 

Pit

There will be one double-sided pit on the course.  Only authorized personnel are allowed access to the pit and must have their pit pass displayed at all times.  Pit passes will be distributed at registration to each competitor (one per entrant) in UCI events (Elite Men, Elite Women & Junior Men and Junior Women).

Pit Box assigments for UCI events will be done in advance by the PCP. Allocation will be available at check in.

In non-UCI events, only those working the pit will be allowed. The pit official will have the authority to remove anyone that is interfering with the proper functioning of the pit.

We will have bike racks in the Pit.  These are for racers that are currently racing, not for storing your equipment all day. Please remove your equipment immediately following your race to make room for others.

Bike washdown for active races will be approximately 50m from the pit with two pressure washers available.

Note: Additional bike washing will be available near registration for racers after their event if the weather dictates it.

Equipment

No flat bars or tires wider than 33mm will be allowed in UCI events (Elite Men, Elite Women). Officials will check tires in the holding pen prior to the start of the UCI races.  .

For racers participating in the singlespeed events, they may either ride a true singlespeed bike (one chainring and one freewheeling cog) or may also ziptie a SRAM-equipped drop bar bike into one rideable gear. Zip ties should be left untrimmed and can be obtained at the registration table. No ziptieing of Shimano- or Campagnolo-equipped drop bar bikes. We encourage elite (non-UCI) racers to adhere to the spirit of the discipline.

Anti-Doping

Anti-doping is under the control of USADA and ITA in accordance with UCI regulations.  The location of the anti-doping area will be located  directly after the line to the right
