PODIUM ETIQUETTE AND CHANGING AREA

Immediately following the completion of each race on both October  2nd and 3rd, the top 3 riders must proceed to the podium area. This includes ALL amateur and UCI events. The podium area is on a raised platform within EVENT HQ. The top three finishers must report to the stage for awards, podium pictures and potential interviews with the professional announcer.

Riders are advised to have podium bags ready prior to the race (a podium bag typically contains a clean jersey and any essentials to prepare for awards and photos). If riders have support staff, they may assist their rider in the changing/preparing but support staff is not allowed on the podium stage. There will be a “UCI Awards Prep” tent located within the EVENT HQ.

Prize money may be withheld from a rider who does not report for the podium ceremony. It is a rider’s responsibility to be present for the awards presentation. All podium finishers must wear his/her race/team kit for podium pictures – please note that riders are allowed additional/warmer team clothing in cold weather. This is your opportunity to support your sponsors and the event sponsors!

 

AWARDS CEREMONY PROTOCOL

• The riders that must report to the podium are the Race Winner, 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th place. UCI podium is for only the top 3

• UCI Elite awards podium ceremonies will be within 20 minutes after the finish of the first rider of the final  race on both days.

• Failure to attend awards ceremonies results in a $500 fine for a C1 event and a $100 fine for a C2 event

• Amateur awards podium ceremonies will be held approximately 15 minutes after the completion of each race on both days. Riders on all podiums are required to wear masks.

POST EVENT PRESS CONFERENCE (UCI RIDERS ONLY)

Riders shall remain in the podium area briefly after their ceremony for potential interviews. Riders should then report to anti-doping if required.

Top 3 athletes should go straight from the Awards Ceremony to the Press Conference. The Press Conference and interviews will be held at the Awards Stage

EventAddress: Weiser River Trail - East Main Street Trailhead, Weiser Idaho
EventNotes:
If you enjoy leisurely bike rides with a wide variety of scenery, join us while we explore Idaho's longest rail trail on this two day 85 mile ride from alpine meadows to desert canyons.  Located in southwest Idaho, the Weiser River Trail runs from Weiser to nearly New Meadows along the former Pacific and Idaho Northern rail line. The railroad corridor is owned by Friends of Weiser River Trail (FWRT), the sponsor of this event.  FWRT is dedicated to providing a unique recreational opportunity along the trail including developed trailheads and a campground to assist trail users. OctoberTrek is an opportunity to experience our rail trail with all the amenities of a supported ride and helps you meet new cycling friends in a noncompetitive atmosphere.

The entry fee includes shuttle for the rider and bike, event shirt, meals, campground tent site and hot spring soak, luggage transportation, refreshments, sweep, and sag support.  Before you register, see the October Trek participant information on https://weiserrivertrail.org/events for more details, including video and photos from past events.

The rider registration fee includes a T-shirt. Riders registering after we place the order on September 20 will receive a shirt at the event only if we have extras available.  The shirt order deadline is September 20.  We will determine the shirt color from what is available from the manufacturer in September.

If you have nonriders accompanying you, additional fees apply to them for camping and hot spring use and each meal the nonrider chooses to attend.  Nonrider meals are limited to Saturday lunch, Saturday supper (includes hot spring and tent camping), and Sunday breakfast. Nonriders are not eligible for Sunday lunch because it will be on the trail.  Contact us for breakout of costs at weiserrivertrail@gmail.com.

Event registration is for tent camping at Mundo Hot Springs. There are optional RV site, a 6 bunk hostel, hotel style room or cabin available at additional cost. Reservations may be made directly with Mundo Hot Spring at 208-257-3849.

Consider becoming a member of Friends of Weiser River Trail. This National Recreation Trail is totally supported by our members along with donations and grants. Members receive updates on trail news and events through our newsletter. Visit us at http://weiserrivertrail.org/membership-%2F-donations for membership links.

REFUND POLICY

If you need to cancel for any reason, please email weiserrivertrail@gmail.com. 90% refund up to 09/13/2025, 50% refund from 9/13 to 9/27.  No refunds after 09/27/2025.

We hope to see you on the trail!

The Big Wild takes place on the the High Country Pathway- the largest continuous single track loop trail in Michigan. A rugged 76ish miles winding through the most remote wilderness in the Lower Peninsula. Attempt to finish by bike or foot.

For Osage Passage Gravel Grinders and Championship Racers

Please see the website for more information.
www.osagepassage.com

This is the 17th year of Going the Distance! This annual bike ride raises much needed funds to support the Boys & Girls Club of Brattleboro. 

The pavement rides are 40, 60, or 75 miles in distance, supported by rest areas in Turners Falls and Greenfield as well as a support vehicle. These rides travel down Route 142 through Vernon and enters Massachusetts, continuing on beautiful country roads until the first rest stop in Turners Falls. From there the 40-mile riders return to Brattleboro, while those on the 60 & 75 mile rides continue through more gorgeous country roads, with the second rest stop along the Green River in Greenfield, MA where lunch is provided. The final leg of the ride brings you back to the Club, where a celebration awaits at our NEYT After Party!

We also have gravel routes available. The 26.8 mile and 38.7 mile Gravel and Gravel Plus routes through Dummerston and Putney offer outstanding riding on quiet New England back roads! With both rides starting and ending at the idyllic Rt. 30 covered bridge riders will immediately be immersed in a quintessential gravel ride.

The 38.7 mile Gravel Plus ride is not only the longer of the two offerings, but the tougher as well. With nearly 5,000 ft. of climbing (and descending!) over all possible terrain (Class IV roads, abandoned roads and single track...as well as loads of beautiful quiet back roads) this ride will challenge the strongest of riders. But don't get too scared -- it is all rideable on a good gravel bike. We recommend 35mm tires or larger.

The 26.8 mile Gravel ride offers much the same as the longer route, but it is shorter, has less climbing and there are no technical Class IV roads, abandoned roads and single track. If you have a bike with 35mm or larger tires suitable for quiet, beautiful tree lined back roads you are properly equipped. Just bring the lungs and legs to ride the mileage with nearly 2,975 ft. of elevation -- some hard but satisfying climbs (You did it!) and the always fun descents -- cruising down the most wonderful roads imaginable.  Then the Gravel ride is for you!
 
 
E-bikes? Sure, bring the motor...we're not snobs! There will be plenty of riders probably wishing they had your e-bike...

EventName: PGC250 Passage to the Past Bicycle Tour
EventNotes:
PGC250 invites you to take a commemorative bicycle tour of iconic historic sites to honor America’s Semiquincentennial in Prince George’s County as we explore the theme of “We the People.” 

WHEN: Saturday, October 3, 2026 from 10:00 a.m. – 2:00 p.m.
WHERE: Patuxent River Park Pavilion, 16000 Croom Airport Road, Upper Marlboro, MD 20772
LENGTH: 25 miles, a cue sheet and route map will be provided
ROUTE: https://ridewithgps.com/routes/56357303 

ABOUT THE RIDE

PGC250 created a bicycle tour for you to learn about the vast array of iconic historic sites in rural Prince George’s County while enjoying a bicycle trip. The route stops at iconic sites that have featured in the history of Prince Georges County such as Selby’s Landing, Columbia Airfield, Nottingham, St. Thomas’ Church, the Rural Life Museum and the Merkle Natural Resources Management Area. Riders will meet at the Patuxent River Park Pavilion and follow THIS ROUTE. (The route may be revised depending on road conditions at the time of the event. All roads are paved, though rural roads may be rough in places. Printed cue sheets indicating the turns will be available at the event.) Experienced volunteer cyclists will ride along with us to assist riders and site leaders will greet riders at each stop to provide information about the history and significance of the sites. Refreshments will be provided at selected stops, and at the end of the tour, which will end with closing remarks. This event is funded by a SHINE grant and was built in partnership with Sankofa Impact. Thank you to volunteers from the Oxon Hill Bicycle and Trail Club for their help and advice.

ABOUT PGC250

The United States Semiquincentennial is the 250th Anniversary of the Declaration of Independence which occurred on July 4, 2026. In 2023, Gov. Moore authorized the Maryland 250 Commission and charged it with developing, encouraging, and executing an inclusive observance of the 250th Anniversary that recognizes all Marylanders’ struggle for life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness before, during, and after the Revolution, and identified three themes – history, civics, and service. 

In Prince George’s County, Anacostia Trails Heritage Area (ATHA), the non-profit management entity of the county’s state-certified cultural tourism district, and PG Parks in the Maryland-National Capital Parks and Planning Commission created PGC250.org to create a space for conversation and collaboration to spark ideas and partnerships to creatively illustrate and interpret our region’s contributions to American history. The theme for Prince George’s Commemoration is “We the People.”

But…What is cyclocross anyway?!

Weellll…it's kinda like if a road bike and a mountain bike and a cross country running event all got mashed together!

Cyclocross is the best spectator friendly cycling event there is. ‘Cross races are held on short 1.5 to 2 mile laps that will mostly consist of grass and sometimes mud but can include sand, artificial barriers, hills, off camber sections, forced runs, and just about any dumb thing we can find in the park to make the race more fun to do but also to watch! We strive to make the race fun for everyone that comes out; from beginners and youth racers to the most experienced elite racers in Arkansas but especially to spectators! SHAM endeavors to make as much of the race course visible from as many spots along the way as possible, but especially at the start/finish line so you can cheer on  your friends and family and all the other racers out for a fun day in the sun…or mud…or maybe snow…but almost definitely sand and grass!

ROJR 2026

Day of Registration  + $10.00

The 2026 ROJR (Ride On Jeremy’s Ride) will be held Saturday, Oct. 3 with riders rolling out of a location near Holmesville, Ohio at 9:00 am.  A 64 mile gravel/paved mix will be for solo riders participating in the Ohio Gravel Race Series. If you are not a serious contender, we encourage you to grab 2 or 3 friends and form a 3 or 4 person team and have some fun with the 38 mile route.  You decide if the 4th person will help or hinder the team. Time stops when your third person crosses the finish line. The Team Event will include some "challenges to be completed" along the way. This route will include about 30% gravel. 

This event is an unmarshalled and unsanctioned event.  We will have limited support and aid on the course so please prepare for the worst.  The course is NOT marked, you must trust your GPS.  It is an open road to other traffic and you must ride according to all traffic laws and signs.  We strongly recommend a reliable GPS unit such as the Wahoo ELEMNT Bolt for navigation.

ROJR 67 mile qualifies for Ohio Gravel Race Series Points

  38 mile route 

      https://ridewithgps.com/routes/48427334

64 mile route 

     https://ridewithgps.com/routes/48509974

The 64 mile route has a good mix of gravel and pavement with some difficult climbs.   You will be rolling thru some of the most scenic countryside Ohio has to offer.  Tires recommendation at least a 32mm gravel tire.  We previewed the course on bikes and our GPS had us at over 6,000 of elevation gain.  The difficult part of the course is from mile 15 - 60 with over 50% gravel total. There will be 2 aid stations with Water & Nutrition.

Description

The ROJR is a “gentleman’s race,” and spans several counties that offer some of the best gravel roads in the state.  You will meander past scenic farms, through shady glens and into areas so dense and deserted you will be sure you took a wrong turn! To finish this route, trust your GPS. Keep a close eye on the weather as well as we’ve seen sleet and 70’s for this event. October weather is uncertain if anything.

The ROJR 38 can be done as an individual event or as a team of three or four. There will be several challenges along the way for time bonuses. 


Check in starts at 7:30 a.m. 
The ride honors the life of Jeremy Grimm. Grimm was a Cat I racer who lost his life in 2017 in a bicycle/truck accident. He left a wife and two daughters. 

 

Food

Light breakfast from 8:00 - 8:45 am

3 aid stations (water, nutrition)

Lunch/Dinner from 12:30 - 3:00    Featuring Chicken BBQ and cold beverages from Bowman Beverages

RULES

There will be plenty of circumstances along the course that will not be covered in the rules. When these circumstances arise, code-of-conduct best practices apply. Let's honor each other as gentlemen and gentlewomen. 

To be considered an official finishing team, and to be eligible for the grand prize and trophy, your team must complete the entire 38 mile course. If your team makes a wrong turn the team must go back to where the team left the route and continue from there. The ROJR 2026 course presents challenges throughout the race! Any portion of the map left unridden will disqualify the team from any awards.

Your team's time will stop when the third member crosses the finish line.

The underlying spirit of this event is to have fun while challenging yourself alongside good friends. The course terrain serves as a team motivator for overcoming obstacles together.

BE THE REASON SOMEBODY FINISHES THE RACE, NOT THE REASON SOMEBODY DOESN'T.

ROJR ON EVERYBODY!

EventName: Women's Cycling Collective: Century Jubilee - 102/51/22mi Women's Gravel
EventNotes:
Women’s Cycling Collective: 

Century Jubilee

Date: Saturday, October 3rd

Start time: 7:45am

Location: Frost Beer Works, Hinesburg, Vermont

 

Come join a community of warm, endurance minded, bright spirited women riders for our second annual Century Jubilee: 100/50/22mi Women's Gravel as we ride through mixed surface roads in southern Chittenden and northern Addison County, starting and ending at Frost Beer Works, crafter of tropical, balanced, hazy IPAs and dedicated supporter of women in cycling.

 

Whether you're experienced with rides of longer duration or have been working to develop comfort and confidence as you build your capacity, there's opportunity here for you. Women's Cycling Collective is focused on offering collaborative, rider-focused events designed to support, encourage and connect women while they explore their potential through the context of the bike and the lens of endurance, training, and the natural world. We invite you to be part of the collective energy that serves to uplift, empower, and inspire women both on and off the bike.

 

Thank you to our generous business supporters and partners for enriching rider experience and making this event possible: Frost Beer Works, Velocio, Burlington Physical Therapy, Julbo, Darn Tough Vermont, Bivo, Bennett Creative Co. and Karen Mulkey Jewelry.

 

General Information: Details, including routes and other specifics are subject to change. All participants will be emailed updated and current information, including routes and course information, in the days leading up to the ride.

  • Full registrations for the 100-mile and 50-mile routes include ride, aid/SAG stops (mile 18, 42, 51, 60, 84, and102), access to personal drop bags and bins to discard layers and gear at each SAG, 2 raffle tickets, commemorative print (for the first 35 registered riders across all distances), Aromas of India meal, and a complimentary Frost Beer Works draught pour. Registration for the 22-mile route includes ride, aid/SAG stop (mile 13), access to personal drop bag and bin to discard layers and gear at SAG, raffle ticket, commemorative print (for the first 35 registered riders across all distances). Meal, served at 11:15am is sold separately for the 22-mile route.

    • There are a number of questions we are asking participants to answer during the registration process. While only some are “required,” responding to all will help us shape the event in ways that better meet individual needs and preferences when and where possible.

    • We ask that you identify with pronouns she or they if you choose to register for any of the Century Jubilee offerings.

    • Registration closes Sunday, September 27th at 9pm. There is NO DAY OF EVENT REGISTRATION.

 

  • Limited number of complimentary commemorative Century Jubilee 8x10" posters:

    • Hand printed and numbered locally at New Duds.

    • Offered to the first 35 registered participants.

 

  • Complimentary Century Jubilee t-shirt for riders who register before Wednesday, September 23rd!

    • Designed and by Stephanie Bennett at Bennett Creative.

    • Sweatshirts available in lieu of t-shirts.

 

  • The route consists of one clockwise 51mi loop that is repeated in reverse (counterclockwise) for the 102mi participants.

    • For women completing the 102, this will provide a sense of familiarity in the second half, with a different perspective and feel since riding in the opposite direction.

    • Since our personal paces vary, many women will have crossover as they complete the first fifty miles and/or continue for a second lap as they work towards one hundred, promoting a sense of togetherness, an opportunity to cheer each other along, or simply share a smile or wave in recognition of our shared experience.

    • The route will be partially marked. Riders are expected to carry bike computers/GPS/phones that can support navigation.

FOR 100 and 50-mile routes:

  • Support and resupply at aid stations and with local business partners is available every 9-25 miles.

  • Check in at all aid stations along respective routes is required of all participants.

  • Each rider will receive an additional raffle ticket at each SAH along their respective route, including the finish.

  • Sunrise is at 7:00am and sunset is at 6:40pm.

    • Mile 0 (start): Frost Beer Works, Hinesburg, VT

    • Mile 18.5: Burlington Physical Therapy tent on Hardscrabble Road - full SAG (nutrition, hydration), drop bag access, and portable restroom

    • Mile 42: Adam's Berry Farm, Charlotte, VT: partial SAG (1 popsicle per ride provided by Adam's Berry Farm, water) drop bag access, farm stand open for purchases

EventName: RISE: Ride. Celebrate. Take Care of You
EventNotes:
RISE: Ride for more. More adventure. More community. More awareness.

Women of OZ Annual Fundraiser

WHY WE RISE

All year long, Women of OZ gives back to women in our community through free rides, skills clinics, education, mentorship, and connection.

We believe more women belong on bikes—and that cost should never be what keeps someone from finding her people, building confidence, or discovering what she’s capable of.

ONCE A YEAR, WE RISE.

Join us for our annual fundraiser in partnership with the Breast Cancer Foundation of the Ozarks (BCFO).

This is our day to:

Ride together | Rally around women in our community |Raise awareness for breast health |Fund the free programming that happens all year long

YOUR TICKET INCLUDES

Guided Experience - choose from MTB Ride, Gravel Ride, Art Ride or Yoga
Eat good food
Enjoy a bevvie
Dance to music
Hear from an inspiring woman
Connect with your community

BONUS IMPACT

Through our partnership with BCFO, every guest receives a confidential mammogram voucher — yours to use or pass along to a woman who needs it.

 

COME FOR THE RIDE. STAY FOR THE PARTY.

Leave knowing you helped create more access, more opportunity, and more community for women in the Ozarks.

Because when women show up for women, good things happen.

 

ONE RIDE. ONE CELEBRATION. A WHOLE YEAR OF IMPACT.

 

Ride Experience Details:

We will have ride leaders for skill levels between Beginner to Advanced. 

If you're new to mountain biking OR have never done a fundamentals skills clinic we REQUIRE YOU to start with the WOZ Fundamental Skills Clinic during registration. Regardless of your riding experience we feel taking this skills course from one of our WOZ certified instructors will help improve your riding and create a better riding experience for all.

What do you need to attend the Flagship?  A mountain bike in good working order (contact a local bike shop for a tune up), helmet, closed toe athletic shoes, flat repair kit, water and snacks.  We also recommend sunglasses for eye protection and gloves.

***Ride levels are based on YOUR CURRENT skills and endurance levels *** We want everyone to have the best and safest experience possible so we’ve laid out a “rating” system to help align you with the right ride group. Please review the skills, endurance, milage and proposed trails.  Being in the right group makes a better ride for all. 

At registration first choose your riding and fitness level, then choose the best description among the groups. Remember if you want to ride with a friend, register ASAP in the same Level AND Group # to ensure you'll be in the same group.  

Choose your group:

FUNDAMENTAL SKILLS CLINIC... this is the starting place
Select this group if you have never ridden a mountain bike,  it’s been a little longer than you would like to admit, OR you've never taken this clinic before….. Welcome!   You have to start somewhere and this is the place!  Even the most advanced riders need to brush up on these essential skills.  This Skills Clinic will cover the fundamental of mountain biking and then you'll hit the trail for a 2-3 mile ride. 

Skill Level 1 

Skills you can perform:
Staying upright while pedaling
Fitness Level- no requirement 

GREEN ….New
You’ve ridden on the dirt multiple times now and you are starting to get the hang of things. You are now putting those skills from the clinic into play and working on shifting, braking, and body position.  Ride 5-7 miles.
Skills you can perform:
Skill level 1+
Level pedals while riding 
Riding with one finger over L & R brake levers
Getting to know berms (those are those turns with the dirt) 
Fitness Level 1 
Able to ride 30 minutes on easy terrain
Climbing a hill on the bike might require a breather break on the way up, and at the top of the hill. (I thought hills were for going down??)

GREEN +.... New with constant improvement 
Here to add the obstacles and steeper hills, but you are taking fewer breaks and pushing the ride time and mileage.  You are attempting more rocky surfaces, bridges and to roll over roots. (Yep we just roll right over those suckers.) Distances up to 8 miles or 2 hours are doable. Down Tristan’s?  Let go up it! Ride 5-7 miles.
Skills you can perform:
Skill level 2+
Standing on level pedals in “ready” position comfortably
Getting comfortable with appropriate gear shifting 
Novice on cornering and berms 
Comfortable crossing bridges 
Okay rolling over low roots/rocks and through tight trees  
Fitness Level Required 2 
You ride 2x a week
You can handle non-stop riding for up to an hour on easy terrain, after that it’s hit or miss.
You can climb up Crystal Bridges hill without stopping, but give me a breather at the top!

BLUE ....Confident and Fit.... attempting rock gardens
The rides are getting longer and the pace quicker.  Getting quicker out of berms you are confident in shifting, comfortable on single track and open to attempting obstacles.  You’re getting the hang of Coler, riding most of Slaughter Pen, and may have ridden Back 40 or at least parts of it. Ride 9-12 miles.
Skills you can perform:
Skill Level 3+
Controlled braking
Must be comfortable cornering and with berms 
Bike-body separation are natural
Comfortable with most moderate terrain (steeper, rockier, wetter, etc.)
Confident with wide switchbacks
Able to look up the trail and anticipate shifting, position change, obstacles, etc.
Fitness Level 3 
You ride 2-3x a week on an average in season week
You can climb longer with soft pedaling as a recovery instead of stopping
You can ride moderate pace for 2 hours with minimal stops 
Must be able to climb Ozone 
Intermediate skill group: here because you’re still working on upping the mileage and ride time. 15 miles or 3 hours might be my cutoff!                 
                              
BLUE +... Confident, fit and ready for a 3hr ride
You’ve been riding for awhile now, put a lot of time and mileage in to riding confidently and tackling bigger challenges are a regular thing. You are comfortable with fast descents, rock gardens, more technical climbs and features.  Ride 10-15 miles. 
Skills you can perform: 
Skill Level 4+ Confident with bike handling skills with roots, rocks, tight corners, etc
Your tires are leaving the ground
Climbing technical terrain 
Comfortable in tight Berms/Switchbacks and exit with acceleration 
Can ride technical single track 
Able to get up and over moderate obstacles up to 6 inches off ground
Fitness Level 4 
Riding 3-4x a week 
3  hour rides are doable
Able to climb continuously without breaks 
Can ride most of Back 40 

BLACK....Advanced rider and can ride with a pro-mtb'r
Ride now, talk later.  You are up for fast paced, intense, challenging, demanding, some good ol light-hearted competition!  Be ready to ride fast, nail some jumps and drops, and possibly get a QOM in the meantime! Ride 15+ miles.
Skills you can perform:
Skill Level 5+
Comfortable with drops and changing technical terrain 
Hop over obstacles  
Able to perform front wheel/rear wheel lifts (up to 6 inches as needed) 
Fitness Level 5  
Riding 4-5x a week 
Considers racing around the Back 40 in around 3hrs FUN
Ready to move at a rapid pace throughout ride
Continuous movement, breaks only to refuel 
Can ride Rock Solid and Schroen Train 

ART Ride - Ride, explore, and experience art! This easygoing group ride follows the greenway while taking in local art and creative spaces along the way. Enjoy a relaxed pace & connect.

Gravel Rides  - Get out, explore, and enjoy the ride! Choose from two group options based on your preferred pace and distance: Relaxed: 10 mph pace, approximately 15 miles or Faster: 12–13 mph pace, approximately 20 mi

Yoga - This all-levels yoga session is designed to help you move, breathe, and reset. Expect gentle movement, mindful breathing, and plenty of good vibes.

REGISTRATION:  If you have a friend on the same ride level that you want to ride with make sure to register in the same ride level AND same group number (register ASAP to ensure this is possible). We will NOT be able to make any changes to groups unless you need to cancel your registration. This is all to deliver the best possible ride experience for each and every one of you! If you don't end up riding with your friends, don't worry, you'll have the opportunity to make new ones and see your other friends at the social afterwards. Win win!

Not sure which group to join?  A great way to know if you are ready to advance ride levels is if you were able to keep up with the ride leader the entirety of the ride and felt like you could have continued at that pace for more. If you are still unsure on which ride might be for you just contact us…..we love talking bikes.

Need a Bike?
Women of OZ is grateful to have three amazing options for mountain bike support at our flagship ride! This option is for WOMEN only on the days noted below.

HUB Bike Lounge - Book your Santa Cruz demo here for 30% off using code WOZRISE2026.

ARI Bentonville - Book your $20 demo here - select Bentonville, AR and click Schedule Demo. Choose either a Nebo, Timp or Signal. Enter code WOZRISE at checkout for a free demo bike on Flagship Day. Optional insurance is encouraged (but not required). Please reserve by 10/1. Every demo bike includes a complimentary Skratch electrolyte mix. Pick-up: at 1:30pm.

Mojo Cycles – Offering rentals for just $25.  Reserve your rental by calling 479-271-7201
on in person at 1301 N. Walton Blvd. and give them code WOZ Flagship. Pick-up: at 1:30pm.

Cancellation/Bad Weather Policy:  If bad weather arises we aim to cancel the ride portion of the event 2 hours prior to the start  of the flagship.  The afterparty will happen regardless of weather. Stay tuned to social media for announcements.

"Just Another Dirty Dozen" is back for it's 9th year.   This is a bicycle ride up the 13 toughest hills in (and around) Wheeling. Just like the Pittsburgh dirty dozen will be keeping points for the top 5 finishers of each hill. It will be a neutral slower paced ride in between hills. Drew Hollis will blow a whistle at the bottom of each hill indicating the start of the race for each hill. A scorekeeper will be keeping score at the top of each hill. Please call out your name as you pass the top of the hill.

Ride will be lightly supported. Helmet required.  Lights Recommended. THIS IS A DIFFICULT AND CHALLENGING ROAD RIDE WITH STEEP CLIMBS AND DESCENTS. RIDE AT YOUR OWN RISK!

The Route is approximately 45miles with +6,500' of climb. The ride should take around 5 hours because of the slow pace between hills and waiting for the rest of the group at the top of each hill.

We will be leaving from the Wheelcraft parking lot (2187 National Rd Wheeling, WV 26003) at 9:00am.  This is the first year we are having the ride on a Satuday.

Pizza, raffle items, and awards afterwards at the shop.

We are open for online registration on BikeReg. Alternatively you could stop in the shop early for a registration discount. $30 in advance $45 day of (cash, check, card).

EventNotes:
Pump Track Time Trial

We're excited to open the Township's Pump Track to residents and riders from around the area for a chance to see how fast they can get around the course.

We'll offer an Expert Line, which includes the track's jump line, and Line A, which uses only the rollers and banked turns.  We will also have use the short circle track for our beginners and strider riders.  

The challenge: how quickly can you get around the track without pedaling? Riders may take a couple of pedal strokes to drop into the track, but once you cross the start timing line, no more pedaling is allowed.

For complete rules, please visit our website.

Parking
Please park in the lot by the Pump Track. Once that lot is full, please park at the Hanover Township Community Center, 3630 Jacksonville Road, Bethlehem, PA 19017. From the Community Center parking lot, follow the trail past the playground and dog park — it's a short walk that leads right to the pump track.

Food
This event will not have food or food trucks available for purchase. We'll provide water for participants. Please bring your own food and drinks for both participants and spectators.

The 666- a mountain bike adventure ride. 66.6km of the most rugged stuff around. There will be asphalt, double track, single track, primitive bike corridors and hike-a-bike. We'll start in Round Top to kick it off with some singletrack, climb up the Escarpment, have some fun in Tannersville, then head over to Colgate Lake, and down Dutcher Notch to end back in Round top. Meant to test your skills and endurance. It's not a race, but put forward as a route to allow individuals to have their own personal challenge. Entrance fee will include some pastry and coffee in the AM and a light resupply somewhere along the route (TBD). E-bikers are encouraged to join! It's about having fun. 

Entry fee pays for resupply food & liquids.

All excess proceeds donated to Round Top MTB Association.

EventNotes:
About 

Join us for the final Prospect Park race of the year in honor of Al Toefield (Kissena Cycling Club founder) and Pete Senia (legendary race official and NYC racing influencer).

Registration 

  • Please register online. There may be Day of reg allowed if there is space.
  • Register online early! The field limits are strictly enforced and most fields have filled up in the past.
  • If you have a chip from CRCA, Prospect Park, etc please use it. It will help speed up the results.
  • You will receive a new bib for this race. No need to use your series number from 2026.
  • Masters, Women, and Juniors race with their category.  Junior entry fee is $10. Women entry fee is $25. Juniors/Women: Juniors use code PPJunior26 and Women/NB use PPWomen26 to receive your discount. If you don't fall into one of these categories, don't use the code.
  • For those without a USA Cycling Racing license ONE-DAY LICENSES are available on Bikereg for $15 .  Please note that one-day licenses can be purchased only by unlicensed or Category 5 Men or unlicensed or Category 4 women.
  • Race day number pickup opens at 5:40am and closes at 6:30am. There are no refunds or credits if you arrive late.

Start/Finish Location

The Start/Finish and registration area is located at the 3rd Street entrance at Prospect Park West.  This is the same location we use every year, about a 1/4 mile past the main hill and Grand Army Plaza.

Prizes

  • Cat 1-2-3 = $500 all cash prize list. 7 places.
  • Cat 3-4 = $200 to top 3 places
  • Cat 5/Novice = Medals. 5 places.

Disclaimer

  • Promoter reserves the right to shorten race distances due to weather conditions and/or time constraints.
  • Promoter reserves the right to cancel, combine fields and/or reduce prize money if minimum fields are not met.

Course Description

3.4 mile loop along the park roadway in Prospect Park. The course features one moderate (big ring) hill and sweeping turns. Although the course is closed to traffic, you will frequently encounter other park users (pedestrians, cyclist etc.), on the park roadway. For this reason all competitors are advised to stay alert and be polite to other park users. 

VERY IMPORTANT - PLEASE READ!

Riders must not enter the "recreation" lane (aka jogger's lane, including the buffer zone) on the left side of the roadway on the west side for any reason.  Riders must not enter EITHER recreation lane(aka jogger's lane, including the buffer zone) on the east side of the park. Any rider entering this lane, even momentarily, will be disqualified and will not be permitted to race in NY Parks for three months and will not be permitted to race in any Kissena Cycling Club event in Prospect Park for one year.

Event Notes – Northeast Velodrome Hour Attempt

Overview

Come test yourself against the clock in the ultimate cycling challenge: the Hour Attempt. Riders will have the velodrome to themselves for a timed session to see how far they can ride in exactly one hour. This is a unique opportunity to experience a historic discipline in a welcoming and supportive environment.

Format

  • Each rider will have a dedicated one-hour track session.
  • We are offering three (3) individual sessions only – space is very limited.
  • Distance will be recorded and published after the event.

Bikes

  • Any type of bicycle is permitted (track, road, TT, fixed gear, etc.).
  • Riders should ensure their equipment is in safe working order.
  • More detailed equipment rules and guidelines will be published closer to the event.

Registration

  • Pre-registration is required through BikeReg.
  • No day-of entries will be available due to the individualized format.
  • Limited to three riders total.

Additional Details

  • Official timing and lap counting will be provided.
  • Standard cycling safety gear (helmet required).
  • Rules regarding restarts, pacing, and rider conduct will be posted before the event.

Northeast Velodrome Member Registration Code

  • If you're a 2026 Northeast Velodrome Member use your code for a free entry
  • If you're a 2026 Grassroots Member use your code for a 50% off entry

Prizes for setting a new record, thanks to a generous Donor

  • $30 if you set a New England Track Cycling Record for Men or Women (two prizes up for grabs)
  • If you set a New Overall Record for New England Track Cycling you'll get an additional $30

USAC

Novice racers may purchase a one-day license (available on BikeReg and on-site for $15). All entrants must display a valid photo ID and USAC license.

Rules

All USAC rules apply. Free lap rule until 5 laps to go. Pit is wheels in/out. Any type of misconduct will result in immediate disqualification and dismissal from the venue, including but not limited to inappropriate verbal or physical threats, acts, language, or gestures. ZERO tolerance.

Transfers

Self-transfer is allowed via BikeReg until October 3 at midnight.

Cancellation

Cycle 66, Inc. reserves the right to cancel, reschedule, or alter the entire event or individual races due to weather, unsafe conditions, or circumstances beyond control. In the case of weather cancellation, every effort will be made to reschedule the event, and all registrations will be transferred. If the event cannot be rescheduled, no refunds will be issued.

Juniors & Kids

USAC-licensed Juniors (ages 6–14) may race in their category; entry is $15.
Kids (10 and under) may ride the loop free of charge. See the schedule above for times.

Parking

Free public parking lots will be available throughout downtown Edmond and will remain open. Access will be monitored by course marshals.

Course

This venue features a unique 1.25 km closed loop with two lanes of smooth asphalt. The course will run counter-clockwise, with the start and finish at the same location.

Join Us for an Epic Day on the Gravel!

The Jersey Gravel Grinder returns in 2026 for another unforgettable ride through the backroads, dirt lanes, and hidden gems of the Garden State. Whether you’re chasing the sunrise or chasing a new PR, this is Jersey’s own gravel adventure — and it’s calling your name. Full Event Details including planned course routes are up on RSGADVENTURES.com.

The Ride: Gravel, Grit & Glory

Our signature JGG routes deliver a perfectly mixed all-surface adventure — from smooth tarmac to gritty gravel, rugged dirt, and maybe even a bit of singletrack on the Mega & Mega XL courses. Expect 45%–75% unpaved terrain, all clearly marked with arrow signs at every turn.

Prefer tech over trail signs? You’ll also get free access to our RideWithGPS event account, with downloadable FIT and GPX files, plus visual and audio cues to guide you every pedal stroke.

Ride Your Way – Enduro Style

This isn’t just a race — it’s an experience. Compete for the fastest combined time on timed segments rather than your total ride time. You’ll see clear signage marking the Approach, Start, and End of each Strava segment, so you know exactly when to hammer and when to chill.
Go full gas or soak in the scenery — it’s your adventure, your pace.

We'll be using a GPS based App to collect teams and provide leaderboards.

Stocked Aid Stations

We’ll keep you fueled and smiling all day long.
Aid Stations every 20–30 miles will be fully stocked with:

  • GU Gels & Chews
  • Hydration Mix, Water & Coke
  • Aid Station 1 features fresh hot pancakes with maple syrup — because every great adventure deserves breakfast on the trail!
  • Aid Station 2 features hot pierogis & pickle juice
  • Plus More Rider Favorites

All stations include toilets and hand sanitizer for your comfort and convenience.

What You Get

Registration includes:

  • Custom Eastern Gravel Series Swag - Custom Sock Guy Socks & EGS Water Bottle
  • Mid-loop Hot Coffee or Espresso Stop (Adventure & Mega)
  • Post-Ride Meal & Prize Raffle Entry
  • The satisfaction of riding Jersey’s best backroads with a like-minded community of adventurers

Our raffle prizes are always top-notch — past giveaways have included helmets, tires, sunglasses, apparel, gear, and more from our amazing sponsors.

Routes

Each year, we change up the routes to keep the adventure fresh. Riders will receive final GPS files before the event.
Check out routes from past editions for a taste of what’s to come — a true mix of challenge, beauty, and pure gravel joy. (Examples from prior year below and see RSGADVENTURES.com to view 2026 planned routes.

The Cameron Crusher is the 3rd and final gravel endurance event of the SSIC Gravel Series in Steuben County. The course consists of primarily gravel/dirt/seasonal roads with paved connectors. There is A LOT of climbing so bring your legs. We want to get you out there for a great time on what we believe to be a great course! The course will be open and traffic will be on the roads, so please obey all traffic signs and rules of the road. There are some steep downhills and some challenging uphills. Be prepared to come to a complete stop for any traffic. You will be timed over 5 segements withing the 50+ miles course. These segments will consist of 2 climbs, 2 descents and 1 longer endurance piece. YOU WILL NOT BE TIMED FOR OVERALL COURSE.

Please reach out with any questions you may have. Gravel bikes recommended. Mountain bikes are capable. NO ROAD BIKES.

Course Map: https://ridewithgps.com/routes/52757972

***Please See the GPX file for route. Please download and save it. The course is not marked, you will need the GPS file or a riding partner.

***There will be a water/food restock at the bottom of Hathaway Hill before you start the climb. Be prepared otherwise.

KING'S TOUR OF THE QUABBIN – Sunday, Oct. 4, 2026 – Hardwick, Mass.

NEW THIS YEAR! Early Bird registration fees ($40/$60) apply until 9 p.m. July 3. After that, registration costs $10 more.

Online registration closes at 9 p.m. Sept. 30. Fees go up another $10 for day-of-ride registration.

PLEASE NOTE: Due to low registration for the metric century, there has been a route change. The link has been updated below.

Bicycle around the Quabbin Reservoir, a pristine jewel in the heart of Massachusetts. Choose from two road routes (64 or 101 miles) or two gravel routes (approximately 44 or 77 miles, each approximately half paved). Not much traffic; plenty of hills.

Start/finish for all routes is at Hardwick Winery, 3305 Greenwich Road, Hardwick, MA 01082. Check-in opens at 6:45 a.m. Start times are flexible, but we recommend century riders and gravel riders start 7:00-8:00 a.m., and road metric riders start 8:00-9:00 a.m. All routes except the Road Metric will stop at Petersham Common.

Routes will not be arrowed. Routes will be scouted prior to the event for road/trail conditions and may be modified accordingly. Final Ride with GPS links will be emailed to online registrants the week before the ride.

Road metric (64 miles, approx. 4900 feet of climbing)
https://ridewithgps.com/routes/42382528
Rest stops at mile 28 (Pelham, 8:30 a.m.-11 a.m.) and mile 48 (Petersham Common, 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m.).

Road century (101 miles, 6000+ feet of climbing)
https://ridewithgps.com/routes/42382603

Rest stops at mile 28 (Rt. 202 in Pelham, 8:30-11 a.m.), mile 58 (Leverett Co-op store), and mile 85 (Petersham Common, 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m.). Road century riders get a $5 credit to use at the Leverett store.

 

Gravel Loop (77 miles, approx. 6000 feet of climbing)
https://ridewithgps.com/routes/47076480

Rest stops at mile 28 (Petersham Common, 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m.) and mile 60 (Petersham Common again).

 

Little Gravel – hard finish (45 miles, approx.3400 feet of climbing)
https://ridewithgps.com/routes/54352597

Rest stop at mile 29 (Petersham Common, 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m.)

 

Little Gravel – easy finish (43 miles, approx. 3100 feet of climbing)
https://ridewithgps.com/routes/54352606

Rest stop at mile 29 (Petersham Common, 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m.)
 

The gravel routes avoid DCR trails. On the Little Gravel route, there's an option at mile 40 to do an easy finish (remainder of route is mostly paved, and the route totals 43 miles) or a hard finish (remainder of route is unpaved, with nearly 300 feet more climbing, and the route totals 45 miles).

Not sure which route is for you? Not to worry -- you can change your selection online at any time before registration closes. You can even wait until ride day and decide in the middle of the ride. Both road routes are the same until the Quabbin Visitor Center, at mile 18. Both gravel routes go to the Petersham rest stop at mile 28. So whether you're on the road or the gravel, you can decide partway how to continue.

Limited to 150 riders.

Refreshments afterwards at Hardwick Winery, with a food truck for the afternoon.

More info: https://sevenhillswheelmen.org/kings-tour-of-the-quabbin/

EventNotes:
Adventure Cycling Association is celebrating 50 years of bicycle travel in 2026. To mark this milestone, we invite you to join the 50TH ANNIVERSARY DROP-IN RIDES, a celebration across three legendary routes.

WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF THE DROP-IN RIDES?
Drop-In Rides are part of Adventure Cycling’s 50th Anniversary. Just as Bikecentennial ’76 sparked a movement 50 years ago, these rides celebrate where we started, what we’ve accomplished, and where we’re going—inviting riders everywhere to share in the adventure.

THE ROUTES
TRANSAMERICA TRAIL – The original Bikecentennial ’76 route that launched Adventure Cycling. Nearly 4,200 miles from Oregon to Virginia, it passes through small towns, farmland, the Rockies, and Appalachians. Dropping in here connects you with the history of cross-country cycling.

GREAT DIVIDE MOUNTAIN BIKE ROUTE – Since 1998, the world’s premier off-pavement route. Over 2,700 miles of gravel, dirt, and rugged mountain passes from Montana to New Mexico. A true test of endurance and adventure, inspiring riders worldwide.

GOLDEN GRAVEL TRAIL – Created for our 50th Anniversary, debuting in 2026. A mixed-surface journey across plains, canyons, and mountains, designed to showcase America’s growing gravel culture and the future of bicycle travel.

WHERE CAN I LEARN MORE ABOUT THE ROUTES?
Visit our route overview pages to see descriptions, maps, and details to help you choose the ride that fits your goals:

  • Great Divide Mountain Bike Route overview
  • TransAmerica Trail overview
  • Golden Gravel Trail overview (launching early 2026)

HOW DO I GET MY ROUTE AND NAVIGATE IT?
Adventure Cycling offers both paper maps and digital maps for purchase:

  • TransAmerica Trail Maps
  • Great Divide Maps

These maps include turn-by-turn directions, service listings, and detailed navigation notes. Once downloaded, digital maps can be used offline on your GPS device or phone.

Golden Gravel Trail Maps – This brand-new 50th Anniversary route will be free to download starting early 2026.

For more information about digital maps, visit our Digital Routes FAQ.

HOW CAN I FIND A GROUP TO RIDE WITH?
Check out our Companions Wanted listings to connect with others planning to ride.

Adventure Cycling members can post on Companions Wanted (become a member, just $2.50/month), while anyone can respond to a post. Drop-In Rides have a dedicated section in Companions Wanted in celebration of our 50th Anniversary.

Sign up here for your 2026 Knoxvelo Membership.  Knoxvelo is a cycling club for everyone: we are here for all riders to support recreation, socialization, and fellowship through bicycling, bicycle racing, and other related activities.  Your membership is good through the end of the 2026 calendar year.  As a member, you agree to abide by the Knoxvelo bylaws and policies, and to sign a liability waiver (you will do this at checkout.)

Your membership includes entry fees to select RaceDay Events rides in the area, free entry to members only events and rides, and reimbursement under the terms of the KnoxVelo reimbursement policy.  RaceDay Events and other reimbursement is contingent upon earning a volunteer credit and wearing a recent KnoxVelo jersey at the event.  

Join the KnoxVelo Team Forum on Facebook for the most up-to-date information on events, rides, and activities.  

If you have a coupon code, select "Club Member" and enter the code at checkout.

Cutaway Girls and Boys Mountain Bike Teams Fall 2026 Season 

Welcome to the official registration page of the Cutaway Girls and Boys Mountain Bike Teams! This is a club activity, with the goal each season being for all Team members to improve their cycling skills while having a great time with their peers and learning from amazing coaches. 

For this fall, practices will be held on Wednesdays and Fridays. Wednesday practice locations will rotate between several Albemarle County trail networks, and all Friday practices will take place at Miller School of Albemarle. Friday practices will also include an optional “Racers Edge” practice group that will focus specifically on MTB race skills and fitness!  

For Team members in grade 5 and above, there will also be the opportunity to compete in NICA Virginia Interscholastic Cycling League races; more details for those races will be shared in the Pre-Season Information Packet.

Fall 2026 Practice Details:

  • Wednesday and Friday practices with small groups based on skill level
  • Practices will be held from 5:15 to 6:45pm
  • Wednesday practices will rotate weekly between local trail networks (Horseshoe Farm, Heyward Forest, O Hill, etc). Exact practice rotation will be included in the Pre-season Information Packet and confirmed in weekly newsletters.
  • All Friday practices will be held at Miller School of Albemarle

Important Dates:

  • Saturday, August 23 - Pre-season Information Packet sent to all registered Fall 2026 team members
  • Week of August 24 - Practices begin
  • Week of October 26 - Practices end
  • Friday, October 30 - End-of-Season Banquet at Miller School of Albemarle

All registered Team riders will receive a custom Cutaway Youth MTB Team Jersey

We are looking forward to another great season!

Please visit our website for venue information and racing requirements. https://www.utcx.net

UTCX is a USA Cycling-sanctioned series and follows USA Cycling’s Competition Category Policy.

Any UTCX category that is not designated as a Women’s or Junior category is open to all riders, regardless of sex assigned at birth. For the 2026 season, this gives riders 10 categories open to everyone, subject to the age and USA Cycling category requirements listed for each race.

Women’s categories follow USA Cycling’s eligibility requirements. Junior categories are based on age and sex category.

Our goal is simple: there is a place for everyone to race at UTCX, and all riders are welcome.

EventNotes:
2026 I Love Gravel Racing Points Series

Everyone, Everywhere, Every distance

3 distance categories

Short = 24 miles or less, Mid = 25-49 miles, Long = 50+ miles

 

A different approach to a Points Series. There will be 2 categories, Male and Female, no age group, NO E-BIKES. Must be a GRAVEL RACE. No minimum or maximum number of races. No specific races, but Premier Races benefit the participant with double points.

For 2026 we have added Clydesdale and Athena categories. In addition, we will have the Fat Tire and Junior categories that were added in 2025. These categories will have a registration fee of $20 and do not include the opportunity to win FREE, or discounted, race entries. It does include your opportunity to win trophies, swag bags and your private invitation to the Champions Celebration. All details for these new categories are listed below.

Our goal is to increase participation in gravel racing. We are not looking for the fastest Champion. We would like our Champions to be passionate, and engaged, in the gravel racing community. With that thought in mind, the person who participates at more races stands a greater chance of being Champion.

Series will run from March 1, 2026 and end on November 1, 2026. You may sign up for the Series at any point throughout the year, but your points will not count until AFTER you have signed up. No retro results.

**Race results reporting are the responsibility of the participant. Participant must report their results to ILGR through an email (ILoveGravelRacing@aol.com) with a verifiable source, such as timing service or results documentation. Results must be reported within 2 weeks of race completion AND by November 1, 2026.**

$25 fee for registration will include your chance at the Championship. You are not locked into one distance. Your registration will allow you to compete in EVERY distance. 

Points will be awarded for your Overall Male or Female finish at ANY GRAVEL RACE, ANYWHERE. However, we have a group of Premier Gravel Races where double points may be earned. Since we have membership internationally, you may race anywhere, at any distance and participate in this Series.

EventName: 2026 Big Bear Lake Trail Center (WV) Merchandise
EventNotes:
The Big Bear Lake Trail Center is quickly becoming known as the hot spot for classic east coast single track. Years of trail development, by experienced mountain bikers have created a trail system that will have you grinning ear to ear. The terrain has everything to offer; gradual climbs, large embedded rocks, tight slaloms, challenging rock gardens, and off the saddle downhills. Almost 50 miles of trail wind through knee deep ferns, soft needle pine plantations, and groves of mountain laurel. Riders of all ages and abilities will find trails to fit their individual riding skills and need for adrenaline. The Big Bear Lake Trail Center is the place to bring the entire family to experience mountain biking at its best.

We make it easy to find your way around. Trail maps will be mailed to online season pass purchasers or you can ask for one at the main entrance.  We also suggest checking out the TrailForks app or the MTB Project app on your mobile device. Trail fees are $10/day or $30 for a season pass. Season passes will be mailed to you. If you choose to buy a day pass - bring proof of purchase in the form of a printed confirmation email or a screenshot on your phone. A staff member will verify that your pass is valid for that day.

All trails may be used for hiking, trail running, and x-c skiing. Trails are closed from November 1 thtough December 31. Trails are open from January 1 to October 31 each year.

Visit our WEBSITE.

Check us out on FB HERE or our events page HERE.

Cyclists enjoying trails at The Big Bear Lake Trail Center may inquire about overnight camping sites in Beaver Creek Village.

We do not close the trails due to wet conditions.

General Information

  1. Trails are open Jan 1 to Oct 31
  2. Both season and day passes must be purchased online
  3. Day fee is $10.00 per rider per day
  4. Season pass $30.00 (BEST VALUE!)
  5. Large color map included in fee.
  6. Children 12 and under free.
  7. Camping available at Beaver Creek Village sites. Inquire at Guard House or Office or online HERE.
  8. Helmets and personal safety equipment required.
  9. All riders must sign a release of liability form.  

Please contact us with any questions: (301) 501-1516, bikebigbearwv@gmail.com

For the first time ever, the Big River Gravel Series will have an overall series payout for the top 3 men and women in the Mississippi distance. In order to be eligible for the payout a rider must sign up for the entire series using the Big River Gravel Series registration page. It is a dynamic payout. If 50 or less riders register for the Mississippi distance series the payout will be $500. For every rider who registers for the Mississippi distance once over 50 riders, the payout increases by $50 per rider registered. Example- 100 total riders register for the Mississippi distance series, the payout would be $3,000.

A rider must complete at least 3 of the 4 events to be eligible for the series.

EventNotes:
Get Ready for Revenant Cross Weekend!
Presented by ATC Racing | DNA Cycling

We're kicking off the Austin cyclocross season with Revenant Cross at Richard Moya Park in Austin, TX, part of the TXCX series so don’t miss it! With CX Nationals in Fayetteville, AR Dec 9–13, 2026, race with us now to earn USA Cycling points and improve your starting position there.

Expect a course that’s as fun as it is fierce – packed with off-camber turns, punchy climbs, and fast, flowy sections that'll keep your heart racing and your tires turning.

Spectators, this one's for you too! This course is super viewer-friendly, so bring your cowbells, cheers, and your best heckles – racers love it.

New to cyclocross? No worries – we’ve got a race category for everyone, from first-timers to seasoned CX pros. Come race, cheer, hang out, and be part of the scene.

Cyclocross is the perfect way to sharpen your bike skills, test your grit, and most importantly – have an absolute blast doing it.

Sign up now, rally your riding buddies, and get ready for a weekend of mud, sweat, and cheers!

Revenant Cross Weekend is calling – will you answer?

Follow us on Social Media to stay up to date on Revenant Cross!

Instagram:  atc_racing_atx

TikTok: atc_racing_atx

Race rules:

  1. Don’t be a jerk.
  2. Abide by all USAC cyclocross rules.
  3. The promoter’s ruling is final.
  4. Gravel and mountain bikes without bar ends are allowed. No maximum tire widths enforced. 
  5. Please inform the finish line judges if you withdraw from the race. 
  6. Awards will be awarded 3 deep in competitive categories. Depending on field size, promoter may expand to 5 deep.
  7. Please patronize our sponsors.
  8. You must check in with the registration staff to be counted in the results.

 

Entry Fees

Entry fee is $40 for your first race and includes any additional races on the same day (ex. Novice riders may also enter the 3/4/Novice field on the same day at no additional cost).  Note: You must register for these at the same time to take advantage of this discount.

On-site registration will be available this year. Entries after midnight on Thursday 10/29 will incur a $10 late fee and may not be included in call-ups. Registration closes 30 minutes before each race wave, so we highly encourage you to sign up as soon as you can. Call-ups will be by crossresults.com.

 

Racing Licenses

All competitive categories require a USA Cycling license to participate. If you do not have a current USAC annual license you can purchase one at memberships.usacycling.org. Licenses are good for a period of one year and cover road, mountain, gravel, track, and cyclocross racing. If you get your license now, you'll be prepared for the rest of the TXCX series.

 

Parking and Directions

Ample parking is available in the lots at Richard Moya Park for no additional fee. Please respect park speed limits and be cognizant of bicycles and pedestrians inside the park. 

 

Weather

The event is rain or shine. Delays or cancellations may be issued at the discretion of the promoter or race officials in the event of severe weather.

 

Mechanical Support

Austin Tri Cyclist will be on-hand with neutral mechanical support all weekend. Conveniently located near the pit in case you need any mid-race fixes.

BIRDEYE ULTRA

UNSUPPORTED. UNREASONABLE. UNFORGETTABLE.

 

 

THE CHALLENGE

Two routes. One starting line. Birdeye.

BIRDEYE 500

Ride the entire Crowley’s Ridge Gravel Trail—twice.

An enormous self-supported journey through the Arkansas Delta, connecting rural communities, state parks, gravel roads, and the full length of Crowley’s Ridge.

NIGHT OWL 200

Ride from Birdeye to Helena and back.

A long beautiful ride through the Delta for those looking to push themselves without committing to the full 500.

 

THE RULES ARE SIMPLE.

Ride the route.

That's it.

This is a free, self-timed, unsupported adventure.

We provide the route, a suggested start time, and a finish line in Birdeye.

You provide the legs, the logistics, the navigation, the snacks, and whatever it takes to get yourself home.

Your bike. Your pace. Your adventure.

THE REWARD

There is no giant trophy.

No cash prize.

No podium.

The reward is finishing something that looked a little ridiculous when you signed up.

It's the satisfaction of covering the miles, solving the problems, pushing through the hard parts, and rolling back into Birdeye under your own power.  

And, of course, making it back in time for dinner.

Finish the route and add your name to the short list of Birdeye Ultra finishers.

FIND OUT WHAT YOU'RE MADE OF.

Ride with friends.
Push the pace.
Race somebody who wants to race.
Or disappear down the road and make it a solo mission.

Use it as training for your next big one, a bikepacking adventure with your buds, or simply as an excuse to do something completely unreasonable.

However you choose to ride it, we're here to stoke the fire.

THE ROUTES

BIRDEYE 500 Route

NIGHT OWL 200 Route

Looking for beta?
Explore the Crowley’s Ridge Gravel Trail route collection.

Important: These are unofficial routes. Route conditions can change. You are responsible for your own navigation, safety, equipment, food, water, and logistics. Trackleaders registration is required: https://form.jotform.com/trackleaders/birdeye26

There is NO rolling SAG.

If you need a bailout, call your bestie.

THE CLOCK IS YOURS.

Start whenever you want.

Leave Birdeye on any date and at any time that works for your adventure.

The only requirement:

Be back in Birdeye by dinner on Saturday, November 7.

That's your finish line.

THE SELFIE BONUS

Hit the Arkansas State Parks along the route?

Prove it.

Post your State Park selfies, tag Studio Drift, and you'll be entered to win prizes.

Ride the miles. Collect the parks. Tell the story.

MORE THAN A RIDE

Birdeye Ultra is part of studioDRIFT's mission to build a stronger Arkansas Delta through outdoor recreation and community.

Your participation helps studioDRIFT continue investing in trails, outdoor recreation, cultural programming, and the rural communities that make the Delta special.

EventName: JM Collingwood Barn Rat Filthy 50 Gravel
EventNotes:
Join us at the historic JM Collingwood Barn, west of Pretty Prairie, Kansas in the beautiful Ninnescah River Valley! The largest barn in Kansas, built in 1913, is a hidden gem and you'll be in awe of its architectural craftsmanship! 

 

The routes will head south from the barn into Kingman County this year, exploring the roller hills, bluffs, and open grasslands between Murdock and Kingman.

The roads in our area of Kansas range from fast hard pack to light sand over hard pack with some stretches of deeper sand that change in firmness with rainfall amounts. We do our best to limit the amount of deep sand, but it is all part of the challenge in the Ninnescah River Valley.

REGISTRATION FEE INCLUDES YOUR CHOICE OF A LONG-SLEEVED OR SHORT-SLEEVED T-SHIRT, A HOLOGRAPHIC STICKER,  A HOMEMADE POST-RIDE SOUP AND CINNAMON ROLL MEAL (MEAT AND VEGETARIAN OPTIONS), AND AN OPTIONAL CRAFT BEER FROM SANDHILLS BREWING. REGISTER BY OCTOBER 14TH TO GUARANTEE A T-SHIRT BY EVENT DAY.

    

YOU MAY BUY ADDITIONAL MERCHANDISE ITEMS IF YOU WISH…Extra t-shirts from this year and previous years' events, stickers, and meal vouchers for supporters that attend with you. 

The top 3 riders of each race will receive a custom award created by talented, local artists. First place will again this year be a one-of-a-kind metalwork barn rat award. Photos of the awards will be posted on social media closer to the event.

After your ride, relax in the spacious barn loft with a traditional Midwest soup and cinnamon roll meal. Brenda's Taco Soup or The Blew Heeler Special Tomato Soup by The Blew Heeler and cinnamon rolls from the Cozy Coop, both of Pretty Prairie. 

Sandhills Brewing of Hutchinson will be joining us with their craft beer for those that wish to partake.

Enjoy the music of John Depew of Arlington post-ride in the loft.

We are raising money for our local non-profit, the Pretty Prairie Community Food Pantry, 501(c)(3), as they are in need of a new backup generator to prevent food loss in case of a power outage. Meal proceeds of each registration go to the Food Pantry and you may also donate to their cause in the merchandise section. We thank you so very much in advance for your generosity.

If you live a good distance from here and wish to arrive the night before, as to not have to drive too far the morning of the ride, there are options for lodging close by! We include a list of local places to stay in the confirmation email when you register, but you can contact us for that list, as well.

Go Nuts Regionals (GNR) eMTB Rules as follows:  1) Maximum 750watts - assistance up to 20 miles per hour - Pedaling assistance only. No hand or foot throttle allowed. Automatic disqualification. Bicycles must remain locked, i.e., no modification of wheel sensor from factory circumference or any other modification to manipulate the factory set speed of the bike.?2) Throttle mechanisms are prohibited.?3) Studded tires are prohibited.?4) It is forbidden to change e-bike during the event even if the rider finishes the event with the same race plate.?5) It is forbidden to recharge the e-bike or battery in the technical zone during the GNR event.?6) Technical assistance consists of the replacement or repairs of any part of the e-bike at the exception of the frame, wheels or battery.?7) Riders age categories are 18 and under, 19-39, 40-49 and 50 plus for Classes; Amateurs, Experts and Open Pro.  8) Riders can only use the battery in place on their bike and cannot carry or switch out an additional battery during the competition.?9) Race course length will be 4.5 - 7 miles depending on difficulty. Steeper climbs and more technical than normal XC will be tested on some courses. Each category will start an hour apart and should be completed within their hour.?10) Races will be conducted regardless of weather conditions.  In the event of rain or other unfavorable conditions, it may be necessary to alter the order of the event schedule, including but not limited to, adjusting the length of the race or delaying or stopping the program completely.  Should a delay occur, every effort will be made to resume the schedule in a timely fashion if conditions significantly improve.?11) No headphones, earphones or sound devices permitted. Horns and bells are permitted.?12) Riders are required to wear the appropriate helmet. Other protective gear is optional; gloves, goggles, elbow/knee guards, etc.?13) Shirt, shoes, and pants/shorts required. Clipless or flat pedals are both permitted.?15) An E-Mountain Bike is a bike operated with two energy sources, human pedal power and an electric engine, which only provides assistance when the rider is pedaling.?16) The course will the taped and marked. Any rider cutting the course will be disqualified.?17) Any behavior deemed in appropriate or unsportsmanlike like conduct will not be tolerated. Verbal or physical infractions will result in a disqualification.

Severe weather policy- Unless otherwise posted, race will be held. Safety of all racers is our main priority. If there is a delay or cancellation due to weather conditions, racers are responsible for checking information posted by director.?The information will be posted on the homepage of website, social network avenues, and via email up to 72 hours prior to the race.

Transfer/Refund Policy-There will be no registration refunds once registration is processed. We will allow transfers to upcoming races. All transfers must be requested 10 days prior and is only allowed for races that were rescheduled. Transfers will not be allowed 10 days before race or after race.

Choose from the Little Smoker (11 miles), the original Chainsmoker (22 miles), or take on the ultimate challenge with the 44-mile ultra-distance event. Welcome to the Third NYC Velo Fire Tower Brevet (FT3)!  A special thanks to the folks that helped us put this together:

The Team at NYC Velo

Search and State All Road Apparel

Chris McNally Drawing Studio

We're following up the success of the first 2 editions of the Fire Tower Brevet (thanks to all of you who took part!) with a new route & 5 new towers!  The new route spends little time in our beloved Hudson Valley, opting for adventures westward.  This new uncharted terrain (by Fire Tower Brevet standards) includes immersion in the New Jersey Highlands, the Delaware Valley, and the Pocono Mountains of Pennsylvania.  The new route for FT3 explores notable areas of Northern NJ & Eastern PA: Hackensack & Patterson NJ, High Mountain Park, Jungle Habitat, High Point State Park, Stairway Wild Area, Hickory Run Forest, Hell Mountain, and, notably, Staten Island.  While there are some lengthy sections of flat terrain, the 5 Fire Tower ascents include gradients, often unpaved, that can exceed 20% (all 5 tower ascents this year are rideable, apologies again for the gut punch that was Mt Beacon).  Though it may be argued that this ride isn't for everyone we've made accommodations so that those of you uninterested in a death march in the mountains can still enjoy a great adventure:

  • The goal of the Fire Tower Brevet is to push the limits a bit of Brevet-style riding and to explore parts of the Mid-Atlantic & Hudson Valley regions that may be off the radar of NYC cyclists.  Scroll down for details of the ride & prizes, and links to the route. The ride is Brevet-style, starting and ending at NYC Velo - East Village (66 2nd Avenue)
  • The 5 Controles (checkpoints) on the route are 5 historical Fire Towers throughout Northern NJ & the Pocono Mountains of Pennsylvania, chosen for their location and bike accessibility, these include:
    • Ramapo Station Fire Tower (Heart hole punch)
    • Buckhorn Ridge Fire Tower (Rectangle hole punch)
    • High Knob Fire Tower (Star hole punch)
    • Pohopoco Fire Tower (Diamond hole punch)
    • Mauch Chunk (Bear Mountain) Fire Tower (Circle hole punch)
  • The "Suggested Route" is approximately 330 miles. Riders are not required to follow the route, only to visit the 5 Controles
  • Riders who plan to participate are required to register here on BikeReg and will be issued a Brevet card (designed by the artist Chris McNally)
  • At each Controle there will be a uniquely-shaped hole punch used to punch the corresponding Fire Tower on the Brevet card
  • Riders will also produce digital proof of successful Controle check-in/route completion (via a GPS/Strava file and/or Instagram/social media photos of themselves at the Controle) to qualify for the tiered Rewards
  • The official ride start is 5:00am Saturday July 11 2026 at NYC Velo East Village though riders may complete their own adventure at anytime between July 11 and 11:59pm October 31 2026
  • This is an unsupported ride – riders are responsible for their own navigation, hydration, nutrition, equipment, and safety - the use of e-bikes, cars, trains, etc are prohibited for Tier 1 & Tier 2 consideration
  • Riders should take appropriate caution riding on open roads, use appropriate lighting for low light or night time riding conditions, and use appropriate safety gear at all times (including helmets, reflective apparel, etc)

 

The Suggested Route:

https://ridewithgps.com/routes/55755950
 


The Tiers of Participation:

  1. Tier 1 Participation: Riders must start and end at NYC Velo East Village and complete all 5 Controles within 48 hours.  Riders may follow any route but may use only 1 human-powered bicycle (i.e. no e-bikes, trains, or Ubers).  Riders who complete the course (starting & ending at NYC Velo East Village) and collect punches at the 5 Controles in any 48-hour period from opening day (July 11) through October 31 2026 will present documentation to Andrew at NYC Velo East Village or by emailing info@nycvelo.com.
  2. Tier 2 Participation: riders complete the course in 1 continuous ride but take longer than 48 hours but less than 120 hours -- for example if they want to expand the route to take 4 or 5 days and visit other locations in the Catskills, or they simply want to stretch the ride across more days (starting & ending at NYC Velo East Village).  Tier 2 Participation will be open through October 31 2026.
  3. Tier 3 Participation: riders complete all 5 Controles on separate visits over any length of time (weeks or months), but always by bike.  Controles may be completed over separate outings and in any order.  Tier 3 Participation will be open through October 31 2026.  

Rewards:

  1. For successful Tier 1 completion: Coleman Camp of Type 3 in Brooklyn has come on board to make custom Musette Bags, available for the first 20 riders to successfully complete the Tier 1 challenge.  Tier 1 winners will also receive a custom Fire Tower Brevet enamel pin and sticker pack.
  2. For successful Tier 2 completion: NYC Velo will send out a custom Fire Tower Brevet enamel pin, sticker pack, & Search and State cycling cap (limited to the first 50 riders)
  3. For successful Tier 3 completion: NYC Velo will send out a Fire Tower Brevet sticker pack (Tier 3 is unlimited)

Additional Ride Notes:

 
Though it's assumed that all who have signed up for this adventure are seasoned and thoughtful riders, riders are implored to make safely their highest consideration when attempting the Third Fire Tower Brevet:
  • Always have appropriate lighting on you and your bike during low or no-light situations
  • Pay close attention to your hydration and nutrition plan & stay hydrated
  • Please be aware of the dangers of over heating/heat exhaustion -- trust that this ride isn't worth it
As of 7/9/26 the hole punches have been Please see below for some course notes from my recon(s) of the route:
  • The hole punch has been attached to the Southwest leg of the Ramapo Station Fire Tower
  • The hole punch has been attached to the Northeast leg of the Buckhorn Ridge Fire Tower
  • The hole punch has been attached to the Northeast leg of the High Knob Fire Tower
  • The hole punch has been attached to the Northeast leg of the Pohopoco Fire Tower
  • The hole punch has been attached to the Southwest leg of the Mauch Chunk Fire Tower
NOTE that as of Thursday 7/9 all hole punches were attached to their respective towers.  It is possible that this may change as time goes on and other punches disappear - if that happens just document your visit to the tower (i.e. Ramapo Station, etc) with a selfie - there is a backup set of punches in the shop and you can get your card punched after the fact, just record the time with a photo (and send it to info@nycvelo.com) for credit of the Controle.
  • Be sure to tag @nycvelo and #firetowerbrevet & #FT3 on your social media posts -- thanks!
  • Be prepared with insect repellent during the ride -- you'll be swarmed by biting insects (flies, mosquitos, etc) on some sections of the route, especially on the climbs where you can't outrun them
  • I again implore people attempting this course to keep the temperature conditions, hydration and nutrition front of mind as there are food (& hydration) deserts outside of the city and major highways and many things close early in the mountains
Extra Credit:
 
Maybe it's because we've been working on this ride for so long, but we have a list of some additional can't miss things close to the "suggested" Fire Tower Brevet route.  Any registered rider who accomplishes any of the items below during their attempt at the Brevet and posts a photo of it on social media (be sure to tag @nycvelo so that I see it) will get a separate Brevet patch:
  • The first “Extra Credit” is so important that it should just be considered “Credit” – visit the High Point of NJ – it's on the route!
  • Grab a coffee or bite to eat at Abraço (81 East 7th STreet in the East Village, @abraco_espresso)
  • Make a rubbing of a Geological Survey Marker at any point on or near the course
  • Add some additional climbing on the ride (but you can deviate from the route if you like) to reach a total elevation gain of 29,032 feet (a form of "Everesting" without the 24-hour time limit)
  • Spend the night camping at a lean-to along the route.
Enjoy the ride!

Please email info@nycvelo.com with questions

For the eleventh year, Yellow Chip Road is going SPOOKY! Formerly know as Ill Kanza, this is a long running grassroots gravel grinder starting and ending in Kansas, Illinois. In contrast to the recent trend of making gravel events smoother and easier, our routes remain as gnarly as ever! Expect varied surfaces including some very rough gravel and stream crossings, rolling terrain, and remote scenery. The 104 mile route in particular has some especially rough and rocky sections, though none of the routes are easy. All routes will be timed, with prizes for the top three in each category of the 3 longest routes. All entries get raffle tickets! As anyone who's ridden here before knows, these roads can be very rough and challenging so come prepared!
