Or register on-site for $5 extra. A portion of the proceeds will be donated to the Kansas Food Pantry.
 
--- Start Time, Location, and Parking ---
 
The 104 mile route will start at 8 AM, the others will start at 10 AM.
Start location is the park at the corner of Front St and Jefferson St in Kansas:
https://goo.gl/maps/gsWhmNRpTs72
There is some parking available at the park, but you can also park at the lot 200 feet to the south on Buena Vista St:
https://goo.gl/maps/oCh9oWZyEEn
There should also be plenty of street parking available. Make sure not to park at the bank since it is open.
 
--- Course Info ----
 
This event will be mostly self supported. Make sure to bring spare tubes, a pump or CO2, tools, and ideally chain quick links. We will have a number you can call if you really cannot continue but for the most part riders are expected to fix problems on their own.
 
There will be two supply tables with drop bag service, supply table A and supply table B. Most courses will only visit one of them. We will collect drop bags before the event that we will run out to each table. We will also have some additional food and water available to all at the tables. There will be two additional supply tables/coolers on the 104 mile course. Here is the mile marker that each table is at on each course:
22: Table B at mile 12.4
33: Table B at mile 22.9
46: Table B at mile 36.1
72: Table A at mile 41.8, table B at mile 62.4
104: Cooler at mile 39.4, table at mile 58.7, table A at mile 91.3
 
There is also a gas station in Marshall at mile 52.8 on the 104 mile course. If you are not stopping at the Gas Station you can turn left on 6th St and cut .3 miles off the course. There is also a soda machine in Grandview at mile 48.3 on the 72 mile course.
 
We will put a sign at every turn that is on a gravel road and not at a T-intersection. The course will also be marked with pavement markings (on paved roads) and flags (everywhere). The flag will always be on the *right* side of the road just *before* the intersection, ignore flags in other locations. The flag will be pink for a right turn, and blue for a left. We will also have maps and cue sheets available. If you have a GPS we strongly suggest loading the course onto it.
 
*The 104 mile course will be completely unmarked.*
 
Keep in mind this event is held on public roads! Obey the rules of the road and watch out for traffic.
 
--- Timing/Ranking Info ---
 
The timer will start at the start time. There will be a neutral start (except for the 104 mile) until the first gravel road, 1.3 miles into the ride. The finish line will be 1.4 miles before the end of the course, near the end of the last gravel road. There will be a checkered flag sign and a person timing at the finish line. This means the timed distances are 44.6 miles for the 46 mile course, 70.8 miles for the 72 mile course, and 102.1 for the 104 mile course.
 
Make sure your number is visible to the timers as you cross the line. If you're not certain if they got you, please stop and make sure.
 
--- Food ---
 
The Kansas Food Pantry is now located at the Presbyterian Church at 304 S Franklin, and the post race meal will be served there (meal must be purchased, but it's cheap).
https://maps.app.goo.gl/vD6sX9paMAogUWFYA
 
--- Bathrooms ---
 
The bathrooms in the Presbyterian Church (see above) will be open.
 
--- Prizes / Raffle ---
 
There will be awards for the top 3 finishers in the Open 104, Women's 104, Singlespeed 104, Open 72, Women's 72, Open 46, and Women's 46 fields.
 
All participants will get 3 raffle entries - 3 sets of two matching tickets. Before the start, place one ticket from each set in the cup in front of something you want to win, and hold on to the matching tickets. After the ride, a ticket will be drawn for each prize from its cup and winning tickets will be taped to the prizes, so check and see if you won anything!

Rapture in Misery: From 24 Hours of Madness to a Mountain Biking Legend

Celebrating the legacy of a race that became a rite of passage

It Started with a Wild Idea

In 2001, a loose-knit group of mountain bikers rolled into Snow Creek chasing something few could understand — and even fewer could finish. A 24-hour mountain bike race. No glory, no fame — just headlights, hills, and a lot of pain. The idea was simple: ride until you can't, then ride a little more.

That first Rapture in Misery lit a fire. And soon, it became more than just a race. It became a legend.

The First Ride – Snow Creek, 2001

There was something gritty and pure about that first year. Snow Creek, typically known for its winter ski runs, played host to a summer sufferfest. Riders took turns circling a course that felt more like an endurance gauntlet than a bike race. People rode through the night, relying on duct tape, drive, and caffeine to hold themselves together.

There were no luxuries — just tents, cold sandwiches, and the sound of freehubs clicking through the darkness. If you were there, you still tell stories about it. If you weren’t, you’ve heard them.

Landahl Park – Technical, Raw, and Wild

After two years at Snow Creek, Rapture in Misery moved to Landahl Park, one of Missouri’s most revered singletrack trail systems. And with that shift, the race found a new kind of identity: raw, technical, and beautifully brutal.

Landahl’s terrain was a whole different animal. Tight turns, sharp climbs, off-camber descents — it wasn’t just about endurance anymore. It was about skill, timing, and knowing exactly how hard you could push without breaking... your bike or yourself.

Some came because they loved Landahl’s unforgiving charm. Others came because they’d heard about this crazy race where legends were made — and sometimes broken. Either way, it was a proving ground, and it helped cement Rapture as a must-do for Midwest endurance junkies.

Crowder State Park – Community Roots Deepen

Eventually, Rapture moved again in 2009 — this time to Crowder State Park, and with that move came a new phase. If Snow Creek was the spark and Landahl the fire, Crowder was where the fire turned into a tradition.

At Crowder, the vibe shifted from wild experiment to beloved annual gathering. The course was tough — don’t let anyone tell you otherwise — but there was something about it that brought people together. The campground felt like a mini-village each year, full of familiar faces, shared meals, and the occasional beer hand-up.

It was here that Rapture’s community really bloomed. Solo riders, team riders, rookies, and veterans all came together with a shared understanding: this race was something special.

More Than a Race – What Made RIM Special

What set Rapture in Misery apart wasn’t just the course, the miles, or the midnight hallucinations — it was the people.

There was something magnetic about the event that brought out the best (and sometimes the weirdest) in everyone. You’d see solo riders grinding out lap after lap with thousand-yard stares, and then laugh at a guy in a tutu sprinting for a handoff. You’d share tools, tubes, and war stories with people you’d just met.

It was more than a race. It was a reunion for the unreasonably driven — the community of “why-not?” people. Everyone suffered, and everyone smiled through it.

The Newest Chapter

Well HEY!  Another of year of the greatest race in the Land o' MABRA (yes, we own our bias).  

Welcome to Baltimore Youth Cycling's Frosty Cross!  We are proud to once again be hosting the MABRA Age Graded Championships!

We’re glad you'll be joining us.  This year we are back at the Agricultural Center: the same great venue and awesome course (can’t wait to see what our course designer comes up with this year).   

This year we are introducing wave starts!

All riders in a wave will start on a single whistle and results that are sent to USA Cycling will be based on the wave, not on the individual categories. Podiums and prizes at the event WILL BE broken out by category. We repeat, All riders in a wave will start on a single whistle and results that are sent to USA Cycling will be based on the wave, not on the individual categories. Podiums and prizes at the event WILL BE broken out by category.

Why are we doing this? For a few reasons – first and foremost, we believe it provides a better race experience for everyone. Riders in races with multiple classes will start based on Cross Results point meaning a rider starting on a second whistle won’t have to work through the slower riders from the first whistle right after their start. For categories with fewer riders, it means a more competitive race and a chance to work on your race-craft instead of riding around the course with only a few riders. Secondly, it provides a better opportunity for riders to earn points and better their USAC ranking. USAC points will be scored based on the wave rather than the individual field. For riders in smaller fields, this means a chance to earn points where no points would have been awarded for the smaller field. For all riders, you have the chance to earn points based on a larger pool of riders (and thus USAC points).

Location:

The Center for Maryland Agriculture is located at 1114 Shawan Rd Cockeysville, MD 21030 about one mile west of I-83. It's conveniently located a few minutes away from Hunt Valley, where you will find hotels, restaurants, coffee shops, and any other services you might need.  We have ample on-site parking.

Looking forward to a great day!!!  We've put an order in for great weather (definition of this may vary by racer).

    2.    Remaining riders will be staged by bib number, in the order of registration.

Those classes consisting of only cat 5 men or cat 4 women are staged by order of registration. All day-of registrants will be staged behind pre-registered riders.

Transgender policy: 

Baltimore Youth Cycling welcomes everyone to participate in the gender category they feel is most appropriate to them, as described in USA Cycling policies: https://usacycling.org/about-us/governance/transgender-athletes-policy

Women may enter any men’s race for which they are eligible by age, category, and any performance requirements. They may also enter categorized races for men that are up to one category lower than their women’s category. Category 1 women may enter men’s races up to two categories lower.

Master women may compete in men’s master's races as follows:

Category 1 and 2 master women may enter men’s events for riders up to 10 years above their racing ages;
Category 3 and 4 master women may enter men’s events for riders up to 20 years above their racing ages.

Results:  Baltimore Youth Cycling’s Frosty Cross is electronically timed. The protest period is a firm 15 minutes from the announcement that results have been posted. Racers are also reminded to make sure their team name is correct in USA Cycling, BikeReg, and on the waiver at the race.

Pit: There will be one double-sided pit on the course.  Please remove your equipment immediately following your race to make room for others.

Course Description: The course utilizes the beautiful grounds of the Maryland Agricultural Center with a balance of pavement, grass, woods and dirt paths. Much of the course winds around the Farm Center and includes hills as well as flats.

Spectating: The course has great sight lines and many opportunities for spectators to get a great view of the action. A central announcer will be located in near the Start/Finish. There will be food and beer for sale at the event and it will be good. 

Tents: The $20 fee for tent space will go to the Baltimore Youth Cycling junior racing program.

Shred the Edge is back for its 9th year!

This is an unsanctioned race located at Camp Edge in Alloway, NJ. Proceeds from this race benefit Ranch Hope/Camp Edge and the Salem County Reactors Composite Mountain Bike Team.

Each loop is just over 4 miles in length with a mix of twists & turns, roots, and some hills. E-bikes are NOT permitted.

Advanced race - 4 laps (approx 16 miles) - this category is the equivalent to CAT 1/2 for both adults and youth.

Novice race - 2 laps (approx 8 miles) - this category is the equivalent to CAT 3/4 for both adults and youth.

Kids race - 1 lap (approx 3ish miles) - this category is for youth under the age of 12. This is the perfect category for racers who are too young to join NICA or who are new to the sport of mountain biking. The course will be modified to avoid technical areas and course marshals and sweepers will be present on the course to ensure everyone's safety.

Wake up lakeside by taking advantage of primitive camping for a small cash donation during race weekend. No electric or water hook-ups. Port-a-potties will be available.

Spectator friendly course!

We look forward to hosting everyone for Shred the Edge's NINTH year!

Greetings!

As 2025 comes to a close it’s time to gather and celebrate the year and start thinking about next. It’s time for our annual membership drive held at Reed’s Cycles (Boise location) on Bogus Basin Rd.

When: Thursday, December 4, 2025

Where: Reed’s Cycles, 2340 N Bogus Basin Rd, Boise

What time: 7-9 pm

Who is invited: all club member, non-members who are interested in finding out more about the club

What to expect:

  • learn more about the Lost River Cycling club

  • meet club members

  • talk about bikes

  • shop at Reed’s Cycles

  • sign-up to be a member

  • try on a Pactimo kit so that you can order the right size club kit (not obligatory)

  • great food and drinks (or at least pizza and beer)

We had a lot of successes in 2025, including: sponsoring our 3rd Annual Eagle Island Cyclocross race, a successful Over the Hill Gravel Grinder in Horseshoe Bend, the largest Cranksgiving Boise to date, the annual Jason Werst Century, organizing the Rhond van Boise, supporting the kid’s race at the Boise Twilight Criterium, organizing the Thorn Creek Gravel and Beer Ride, hosting weekly road and mountain bike rides, and hosted indoor rides all winter long.

For 2026 we plan on being back for all of these events, plus we’ve hoping to grow our weekly rides! We want more participation and more options for members. Part of 2026 will be reorganizing the club in the hopes of a larger involvement by a larger group of club members.

Come to the party on December 4th to learn more about the club, meet people, and talk about how you’d like to participate in club events. We’ll have pizza and drinks. It’s going to be a good time!

THE 2026 GRAVEL GOBLIN IS ON!!   We're getting in one more trick-or-treat ride the day after Halloween. 

Sign up and ride with the Mohawk Hudson Cycling Club on Columbia County's magnificent gravel roads.  See the stunning autumn colors from the beautiful heights and rural valleys of this great gravel riding area. MHCC members and other cycling enthusiasts ride here all year and keep coming back for more.  PLUS, the first 130 who visit the registration desk will enjoy a sweet surprise treat from Bountiful Bread!!  Register soon, before the end of September, to avoid the $5 bump in the registration fee.

The four routes offer a full variety of ride types and challenges. About the Regional Food Bank:

The Regional Food Bank has been helping to feed the poor and hungry in our communities since 1982. It is the only organization of its kind in northeastern New York. The Food Bank collects large donations of food from the food industry and distributes it to charitable agencies serving hungry and disadvantaged people in 23 counties. From Plattsburgh to Newburgh, in urban, rural, and suburban communities, the Food Bank provides over 55 million pounds of food a year to 1,000 agencies. The Food Bank is a member of Feeding America, the national network of food banks. The Regional Food Bank is a non-profit organization, and all donations are tax-deductible to the fullest extent of the law.

Sunday November 1st 2026 is going to be a day to remember. We’re proud to bring you Cyclocross at Grand Island's premier Beaver Island State Park for yet another year. This place has all the goods including WNY’s best cyclocross sand pit, mixed riding surfaces, rolling terrain and beautiful waterfront views. Can you ride the beach? There’s only one way to find out! The history of Cyclocross at Beaver Island goes all the way back to Brenden Conway's Beaver Island Black Out! in 2012, No one who was there that day will ever forget that experience... 

Join us for a great day on the bike or spectating with friends and family. Beaver CX is not USAC Sanctioned so you do not need a race license to participate. Why would we do that? No reason not to come out of retirement if you happen to be an “experienced” racer that hasn't renewed their license for a couple years. The Stump Farm Mountain Bike Races are back for 2026 on November 1.   The 20 mile, three lap comp event starts at 10:00 and the one lap race starts at 10:10 for the FAT BIKE Category and 10:15 for the one lap 7 mile..  We have a mix of two track trail for passing and leaf blown single track on a full 7 mile plus loop. The Race direction in 2026 generally follows for the Normal trail flow; Counter Clockwise on the map with some added 2 track for passing early in the loop.

This is a small race with field limits so register early. Accordingly, there are no refunds for any reason.  Your registration is final. There are overall and age group awards.

Number plate pickup and concessions are inside the lodge.  We need the number plates back for the 2027 race.  Please help us with that!   

We ask you to self-seed in your start and be aware that the first transition to single track comes after a 0.8 mile roll out just like our August race, Refo Ramble.

We will leaf blow the course on Saturday, a bonus for all our area riders!  There are no aid stations.  We will have mobile course marshals and a medical cart.  

So, bring your own feeds for the race.  We will have Ahnapee Beer free if you show us a trail pass.  Garbage is carry in, carry out. 

Brown County is great at maintaining our trails with the help of the Friends of the Reforestation Camp Trails, one of your hosts!. To ride the trails, the County requires a daily or annual pass. For your convenience, if you don't have an annual pass already, you can pay us $5 below and show the ranger your receipt if you are asked. Otherwise you can buy a pass online or on site on race day or at the sign board just outside the lodge with a card or exact change. Trail fees support the trails.  We like that!  We will give you a beer/coffee ticket if you show us a trail pass as a thank you.  

Course marking will occur Friday to reinforce normal flow. There is no foot race this year.

The event host is the Green Bay Trailblazers, with Friends of the Reforestation Camp Trails,  and Ashwaubenon Nordic Ski Team partnering again.  Your race volunteers are the from FoRCT, Trailblazers and ANST.

Cyclocross is a fun and physically demanding type of bicycle racing. The race will keep your heart rate up, and your bike handling skills on point.

It's Heidi Rentz & Zander Ault here...

We are co-creators of The Spirit World 100 & The Cyclist's Menu, gravel cyclists, chefs & party animals. We're so freaking excited to see you in Patagonia, Arizona for a gravel road race that has inspired every aspect of our lives.

The Arizona Borderlands are known for it's rugged, stunning landscapes & views that you'd never guess existed. You have to see it with your own eyes! Throughout the Spirit World 30, 50, 80, & 100 mile courses - you'll climb up + down & around elevations that range between 4,000 - 6,000 feet above sea level. EventNotes:
Welcome to BikeReg Online Registration

Registration is OPEN !!!   

(Registration Closes Thursday 11/05/26 8am)

for

11th Anniversary of Nevada County Women's MTB Skills Clinic and Camp  

This is a 2 day MTB skills clinic, 

or 

a 1 day MTB skills clinic with an add-on option Sunday for advanced skills

Spread the word!   

Before starting on-line BikeReg registration, determine your rider level from the program.pdf and read our refund policy.

 

With miles cross country and enduro trails, and home of TDS Enduro, TDS Ranch is our venue choice for learning mountain bike skill clinics designed to inspire, strengthen, build confidence and show that mountain biking is a sport for everyone!  Mountain biking enriches your mind, body, soul and opens the door to meeting more women in the biking community.  Learn bike handling skills, increase your confidence, enjoyment learning with others, and trail love when riding your bike.  We raised the bar with Specialized Bike demo bikes available at our clinic!

Proceeds support Nevada County youth bike clubs (~400 youth) and Gateway Bike Park Phase 2 Build in Penn Valley, California.

Our amazing 2026 coaching cadre:

  1. Pro Racer Amy Morrison, National and World Titles, NICA Nevada League Head Coach, Carson City, Nevada
  2. Pro Racer Tasha Thomas, California Enduro Series OA Titles, USA Cycling Coach, S.Lake Tahoe, California
  3. Kristen Del Campo, BICP Certified Instructor, Kings Beach, California,
  4. Lauren Kress, MTB Experience, NICA Coach Certified, Grass Valley, California,
  5. TBA

We have a robust program for women to improve their learning experience at various skill stations, each with various background to teach beginners the basics, and fine tune those missing tiny improvements for advanced riders.  You'll feel more confident off or on your bike, you’ll fine tune bike handling techniques, body positions for various riding conditions/features, and more.  Enjoy our healthy snacks, gourmet meals, and our Nevada County hospitality.  Plus our raffle drawing!  See clinic & meal photos at our FB album:

https://www.facebook.com/NevadaCountyWomenMTBCC/photos

Our instructors are from northern California and Nevada who instruct and coach, race downhill, enduro, cross-country, cyclo-cross, and part of the movement connecting school bike club youth to learn that mountain biking as an awesome sport.  So ..... plan ahead to enjoy a weekend to build your mountain bike skills and network with more shredders who have the dirt passion !!!   Start your list of questions like you hit a wall and can't get to the next level for rides, racing,  nutrition, etc. for our cadre.   We understand this is an expensive cost and we need to pay our instructors and event costs.  Please review the below 2026 MTB Skills Clinic Fee Schedule:

  • $275 Saturday MTB Skills Clinic and Meals
  • $250 Saturday MTB Skills Clinic and No Meals
  • $175 Add-On Sunday MTB Skills Clinic and No Meals (Saturday MTB Skills Clinic Required)
  • $30/night Optional dry camping at venue for RV's, vans, trailers, tents (bring your own water, potty rentals at venue)
  • MTB skills clinic includes, instructors, fees, t-shirt, permits, insurance, rentals, supplies, venue, meals (or no meals).
    • Note:  If you change your mind about meals or add-on Sunday MTB skills clinic sign-ups, please bring cash.

 

Complete custom questions for meal prep!….This helps have an organized weekend from event pint glass order, meal planning, and those dry camping Friday and/or Saturday nights (3pm Check-in).   PLEASE answer ALL questions so we meet your special dietary needs.   Meal plan is weather dependent.  Saturday and Sunday MTB clinics start at 9am.  This allows participants to eat a hearty breakfast at home or on the road.  

 

Click event webpage link for tentative weekend schedule and meal details in the weekend program.pdf. at: https://ybonc.org/events/mountain-bike-clinic/

 

Last but not least, there is poison oak along sections of TDS trails even in the fall and winter (branches with no leaves).  Bring extra shoes/clothes to change out of in case you rubbed against any vines or branches, and plastic bags for post ride clothes for wet clothes.  We will have TechNu packets at registration table.  We have outdoor heaters to keep you warm on breaks too!

 

Swag Stuff!  Oh yeah, our swag bag is loaded.  2 raffle tickets (drawing on Sunday) with bike industry products from our sponsors.  Raffle is U-Pick!

 

This weekend is all about you … Rain or Shine … So Let’s Roll Ladies on 2026 Nov. 7-8 !!!

Requirement:  Complete registration, event waiver, bring bike, helmet, gloves, water bottle/hydration system, water proof or poncho to stay dry for wet weather trail conditions, camping chair, layers of clothing to stay warm (jacket/gloves/hat/neck gaiter) around campfire.   We have propane heaters and canopies to keep us warm and dry when not riding.  When was the last time your bike was serviced?  If your bike has not been serviced recently, please have your bike inspected at your local bike shop to prevent mechanical issues during the event weekend...brakes, chain, tires, etc.  

 

Volunteering?  

Unfortunately registered participants cannot sign-up to volunteer.  From past clinics, participants forget or arrive late for volunteer tasks.  We want you to learn as much as possible from our MTB instructors.  Volunteering does not waive or reduce registration event fee.  Volunteers for clinic groups required to be a intermediate rider and know TDS trails.

 

Note: 

  • We recommend Best Western Gold Country Inn (or a new Holiday Express if open),, Grass Valley
    • More lodging options:
      • https://www.nevadacitychamber.com/nevada-city-hotels-and-lodging/
  • Full RV/Camper Hook-ups at:
    • https://nevadacountyfair.com/rv-park/
    • https://inntowncampground.com/
  • This is a USAC sanction event as a training clinic

 

Participant Waitlist:

Yes, we have a waitlist option at BikeReg registration.  Only add your name to with waitlist if you are sure you can attend.  Because on-line BikeReg registration closes on 11/05/26 Sunday, call (530) 513-7852 so we can confirm you will be attending if a spot opens up.  Please bring cash when you check-in Saturday morning and complete participant event waiver.   

 

Refund Policy:

Why do we have a cancellation policy?
This event is a fundraiser for YBONC Foundation Programs supporting rural Nevada County youth.  We do not issue refunds or transfer registrations for our fundraiser events.  An event participant's registration can be reimbursed as a comp code toward the following year skills clinic, or as a donation to our foundation.  Our cancellation policy reflects the fact that the closer it is to the event dates, the more challenging it is to adjust plans, and the less likely to find someone to take an open spot.  

For any registered participant unable to attend due to injury, illness, or personal reason, please forward your event registration confirmation email to us AND request for the following year event's comp code or state you would like to donate your event registration to our foundation.  Please send individual email per participant, not combined participant emails, to:
Send email to:     yboncfdn@gmail.com
Subject Line:  
Cancellation Notice for MM/DD/YY of First & Last Name of Participant - Request Comp 
Code or Making a Donation


We set event dates a year in advance with clinic instructors, land owner, and plan locations dependent on trails, weather, fire, etc. to create an exceptional experience for every participant, and set things up with the 
expectation that each day will be fun with MTB skills and networking.  We are focused to host a great 
mountain bike skills clinic for women.

•    If severe weather or fires cancels event, participants will receive a BikeReg event cancellation email.  Event cancellation are posted on event FB/IG feeds too.  If forecast is light rain, we will still host event as we have canopies and propane heaters to keep participants warm and dry during breaks and meals.  This is the only case we issue event registrations to participants. 
•    No refunds as event payments are made in advance for costs such as insurance, permits, instructors, product orders, swags/bling, food, instructors, etc.  A registered participant may outreach to someone to fill their spot and arrange payment method themselves, or gift their entry.  Please FORWARD your confirmation BikeReg email with the person's info who is replacing your spot (First & Last Name, cell no. and mailing address.)   

Disclaimer:

As event planning occurs a year in advance, the event organizer is authorized to change event details.  It is the participant's responsibility to revisit the event webpage for latest details 1 week prior to the event weekend.

 

Thank you! 

Jet Lowe,

Event Organizer

Birdeye ’26 is fun-filled weekend in the heart of the Arkansas Delta—where remote gravel roads, big skies, live music, and good food come together for one unforgettable experience. 

Whether you're looking for a challenging ride or just a reason to casually explore somewhere new, Birdeye is your invitation to come see the Delta differently. Check out this slideshow. 

COME FOR THE ADVENTURE

Choose from multiple gravel routes designed to showcase the unique terrain, quiet roads, small communities, and beautiful landscapes of Crowley’s Ridge. From first-timers to experienced gravel riders, there's a route for you. Ride hard. Ride curious. Ride somewhere unexpected. Check out this route collection.

STAY FOR THE PARTY

Come back to the farm for food, drinks, music, and a proper Delta weekend.  Two nights. Two artists. One unforgettable setting. 

FRIDAY · WILL COPPAGE 

Americana, Delta storytelling, and soulful songwriting. 

SATURDAY · BEAR RYAN 

Texas country, Delta blues, and Southern rock ’n’ roll. Small crowd. Big music. Under the Delta sky. 

WHY BIRDEYE? 

Because some of the best adventures in Arkansas happen over here. Birdeye is hosted by studioDRIFT, a nonprofit working to  expand access to outdoor recreation throughout the Arkansas Delta. Your participation helps support the Crowley’s Ridge Gravel Trail and the people and places that make the Delta magical. 

Come for the fun. Stay for the weekend. Leave changed.

The Event

Address - 2813 Jerusalem Mill Road, Kingsville MD 21087

6 Hours at the Mill is a 6 hour individual, duo or team relay race. If you are looking for a fun, laid-back, low-cost, competitive experience where the proceeds go to a few awesome non-profit organizations, then sign up before we reach the 150 racer cap. The approximately five mile long course is challenging but approachable for all ages and skill levels.

October Quiz and Lottery to Win 50% Off Registration

The October quiz question can be found at https://forms.gle/gLCH3htLUSacNMX16 . Each person who answers the question correctly will be place into a lottery. The person selected from the lottery will win 50% off registration or be refunded 50% of the registration cost. This final quiz also contains a bonus question for a second entrance into the lottery. Good luck!

Social Media Updates

For updates please see our Facebook page at https://www.facebook.com/6-Hours-at-the-Mill-100083232973843/ 

Volunteer

Not racing, but want to volunteer. Sign up at https://volunteersignup.org/HBEH7 

It takes a lot of volunteers to make this event happen and we can really use your help with parking, registration, and course marshalling.

Food Truck

Kooper's Chowhound Burger Wagon will be on hand to serve up an assortment of hand held burgers including vegetarian options. You can find them at http://www.brgrwagon.com/ 

The Course

The course is a roughly 5 mile loop with 588 feet of climbing per lap. The course starts relatively flat in the rolling fields of Jerusalem Mill and then narrows a bit as the course gains elevation as it enters into the wooded mixture of singletrack and doubletrack. The course consists of rugged classic East Coast single track. Roots, rocks, significant elevation gains, stream crossings, etc. make for a technical challenge on the first leg of the course. Second half of the course is mostly downhill and / or flat giving a reprieve before returning to the pits and starting the roughly 5 mile loop over. Pits and start / finish area will be in grassy open fields. 

Preliminary race lap information can be found at https://www.trailforks.com/routepopular/81337289/ This is close to the final course, but there will be a few slight changes. The file will be updated to reflect any changes to the course.

Race Duration

The race begins at 9:00am EST with a mass wave start. All solo, duo, and team races are the same duration. Racers, or teams of racers, will complete as many laps as possible by the end time, 3:00pm EST. Racers in the same field with the same number of laps will be scored based on lowest total elapsed race time.

Team Pits

Solo, Duo, and Teams may set up a pit along the course in the field. Team tents (EZ-Up style canopy tents) are permitted, but please take care to anchor tents sufficiently if there are strong winds forecast on race day. Pit selection will occur on a first come, first served basis. While a food truck will be on hand, please be sure to bring enough water and food for the duration of the event.

Relay Transitions

Duo and Team categories are relay races. Scoring and timing will not identify individual racer by name so if you want to know your individual lap times you must keep track of which racer completed each lap. Racers may “tag” their teammate in the pit area but the incoming racer must start at the same location as the exiting racer and pass the “baton.” Duo and team racers may race in whatever order they like (example: Racer 1 could do 2 consecutive laps, followed by Racer 2 who does 1 lap, followed by Racer 3 who does 3 consecutive laps).

Podiums

Prizes for the winner of each class, custom 6 Hours at the Mill medals for the top 3 finishers. Men and women open solo cash payout for Top 3.

Payout for open men and women is $150/$100/$50 for 5 or less registered racers and $200/$150/$100 if there are 6 or more registered racers in the category.

Podium presentations will begin at 4:00pm

The Non-Profits

These events are a partnership between JAMSQUAD Cycling and the Gunpowder United Mountain Bike Operators (GUMBO). Proceeds from the events will support three nonprofit groups: JAMSQUAD Cycling which provides refurbished bicycles for underserved youth and those in recovery and GUMBO whose mission is to develop and maintain a world class trail system at Gunpowder Falls State Park. A donation will also be made to the Friends of Jerusalem Mill. 

Parking

Parking will take place in the fields near the start/finish area. Racers may drop off items for their pit and then move their vehicle to the designated parking area. Please follow the directions of parking volunteers and use caution when crossing the road.

Partners

6 Hours at the Mill would not be possible without our amazing partners: Gunpowder Falls State Park, Friends of Jerusalem Mill, Independent Brewing Company, Bike Doctor of Bel Air, Kiddie Academy and Trek Bicycles.

Weather Policy

Gunpowder Falls State Park and the Friends of Jerusalem Mill generously allows us to race on these wonderful trails.  With their permission, the race will proceed if there is light rain. If there is heavy rain preceding the start or forecast for race day, the race will be postponed until Saturday, November 14, 2026. This race is a fundraiser (see above). In the event of inclement weather on both dates, the race will be cancelled. Please consider your registration fee a donation to the non-profit organizations.

Common Courtesy

Please be respectful of the environment and its inhabitants. We would like to remind everyone that we all have a responsibility to leave the race course cleaner than we find it on race day. All refuse should be discarded into appropriate containers. Any rider found illegally discarding objects in the park, the roads leading to and from the race course, and the on the race course itself will be dealt with accordingly. Trash containers will be available for rider’s to use around the property.
Sportsmanlike Conduct

The Race Promoters expect ALL spectators and riders to act like responsible adults. Use of profanity and blatant unsportsmanlike conduct will not be tolerated. This is a public park and family friendly event, so please be courteous to all volunteers and each other!

Close out your riding season with a ride to remember at Mohonk Preserve! 

Join us for an epic fundraising ride across the Shawangunk Ridge, just 90 miles north of Manhattan. Pick from two distances 50.4 miles (4,711 ft. gain) or 23 miles (1,811 ft. gain). Both courses begin and end at the Ulster County Fairgrounds and once you enter the Preserve at mile two, the course is over 98% gravel on our famous network of historic carriage roads.  

This is not a race; think of it as a super challenging fun ride for a really good cause. Some of the gravel is rough and steep in spots. Expect some loose rock – especially on the descents. The long course includes an optional short technical section and a mandatory dismount/bike hike up a rustic steps near the “million dollar view.” Bring your gravel, cyclocross, or mountain bike. Class 1 e-bikes only are permitted if you can manage the technical sections. No road bikes, please.

You won’t be timed but you will be well-fed. Look for well-stocked aid stations with water, Skratch hydration and energy bars and bananas. A post ride party with food and music awaits you at the finish. Be sure to carry some food and water, and maybe extra clothes depending on the weather - this is a rain or shine event. You’ll be sharing the carriage roads with hikers and climbers, so bike bells are highly recommended. Be courteous to hikers and other riders when passing. Pack a spare tube, tools, and pump as there’s no mechanical support on course and no sag wagon. Helmets are required.

*Shout out to our friends at the Open Space Institute for granting us access to the River-to-Ridge Trail and to the Mohonk Mountain House who grant us special access to Sky Top and the golf course area for the event day only. Bikes are not allowed on carriage roads near Sky Top so you cannot pre-ride these sections of the course. No exceptions – If we blow this, access to Sky Top and the golf course will not continue. PLEASE DO NOT POST PICS FROM SKY TOP ON SOCIAL MEDIA PLATFORMS.

Also, near Spring Farm Trailhead, the private driveway near the Slingerland Pavilion, the Table Rocks Trail, and the Crag Trail on the Preserve are accessible to ride participants during the event only. You cannot pre-ride these sections.

Pricing (No price increase for 2026!)
50.4 Mile $150
23 Mile $125

Optional fundraising: (New!)
When you register you'll be set up with a fundraising page automatically. Raise $150 for Mohonk Preserve and we'll reward you with a super cool Grit pullover hoodie. Money raised will help us provide educational programs for children, maintain and repair the carriage roads you'll be riding on, conduct research and fight invasive species. 

Registration fees get you...

  • Pre-ride bike support on the morning of the event from Bicycle Depot staff
  • Bike plate
  • Grit sticker
  • Aid stations with, water, Skratch Labs hydration products and snacks
  • Finish line food, live music, beverages and beer.
  • A GRIT tech t-shirt.
  • A chance to win great prizes from our sponsors!
  • A gravel ride that's actually on gravel!
  • Satisfaction in knowing you're helping to raise money for a great cause!
  • Timed Strava segment for 50.4 mile course riders with prizes!


The Start
Expect a calm and controlled mass start for the 50.4 mile course at 8:30 am and the 23 mile course at 9:30 am. Riders will line up Goldilocks style: strong riders go to the front of the pack; moderate folks aim for the middle, and those planning a more leisurely pace, head to the back.

A pace car will lead riders for the first two miles of the course along public roads from Ulster Fairgrounds to Mohonk
Preserve property on Gatehouse Road.  Riders must remain in their lane behind the pace car. We mean it, calm and controlled.  

Once you’re off the public road and on the gravel, you can ride at your own pace.

*NEW Cutoff Time for 50-Mile Course*
Cutoff time for the 2026 ride is 2:00 pm at mile 31. If you don't think you can ride at this pace, we strongly encourage you to sign up for the 23 mile course. We want you back at the finish line in time for the the fun! Prize drawing will be at 3 pm. You need not be present to win, but we hope you'll be there! Note: The event takes place after daylight saving time ends so sunset is at 4:44 pm. 

Cancellation/Refund Policy:
Registration fees are non-refundable. You may wish to take the optional Registration Protection Plan from Allianz during registration. Shawangunk Grit is a major fundraiser for Mohonk Preserve. When you register, we hold a spot, make commitments to vendors, and deny others entry when the event sells out. Therefore, registration fees are non-refundable. We do allow transfers for a nominal fee. Event deferrals for any reason, including injury, are not allowed.

Should the event be canceled for a qualifying reason by the event producer such as adverse weather conditions which would make holding the event unsafe, your registration fees will deferred to the next year. 

If you find you can’t participate, we would like to know. Please contact us at shawangunkgrit@mohonkpreserve.org. All cancellations will be acknowledged via email.

About Shawangunk Grit: 

The ridge where you’ll be riding is made from bedrock called Shawangunk Conglomerate, also known as Shawangunk Grit. Shawangunk Grit slabs were used to make millstones around the turn of the century and some of these millstones can still be seen on the land today. A nod to the history of the ridge is found in the Shawangunk Grit logo.

SafeSport

The PanAm Championships and DCCX organizing committee support the goals of SafeSport in protecting athletes and ensuring a positive environment for athletes, supporters and fans. 

Implementation of SafeSport protocols is the responsibility of the officiating crew. No person listed on the SafeSport Centralized Disciplinary Database is permitted in the pit area or team zones. Please provide the names of pit staff during check in (if different from staff you listed when registering). For non-U.S. support staff, a cycling federation license is required. Please present names of support staff and license numbers (if applicable) at registration. Specific questions about SafeSport guidelines pertaining to your support staff can be directed to the UCI or USA Cycling official in charge of pit pass allocation.

Licensing Requirements: All riders competing in the Pan American Championships, Masters Pan American Championships, and/or UCI C2 races must possess a current UCI International license.

If you currently do not hold a license of any kind the UCI license for an adult is $240.

If an athlete currently holds a USA Cycling domestic license, then you are able to purchase a UCI license add-on at a cost of $130 (the price difference between a USA Cycling license and the fee for a UCI license). You are eligible to purchase this add-on up to 30 days prior to an existing USA Cycling membership expiring. Per USA Cycling: this UCI license supersedes a domestic license and thus your domestic license will show as expired once the UCI license add-on is purchased.

The UCI/International license is valid for both UCI categorized races and any local/grassroots races.

More details available here: https://usacycling.org/get-started/bike-racing-for-adults

All riders in the DCCX amateur races must possess either a valid USAC license, a one-day USAC license or a UCI license with cyclocross coding. Non-US citizens must possess a valid UCI International license for insurance purposes. Non-US citizens from Canada can possess a Cycling Canada License.*

*If registering with a license from Canada is not an international (UCI) license, then applicable riders will be required to show proof of insurance that covers them while racing in the USA or sign a waiver acknowledging responsibility for all medical costs they may incur. USA Cycling's insurance does NOT cover riders with only valid domestic licenses from their respective national federation. Foreign federation UCI licenses are to carry with them proper medical insurance, but a Foreign Permission Letter (FPL) is required for it to be in effect. If no FPL is available, the rider is responsible for obtaining travel insurance that covers them while racing in the USA, and they accept full responsibility for medical expenses they incur.

Eligibility for all Continental Championship categories:

  1. The nationality as listed on a rider’s license in the UCI database must be a member of the PanAmerican Confederation.
  2. For Championship events other than Masters, riders with dual citizenship or who have changed nationality in the last year must respect UCI 1.1.033 B.

Masters Pan American Championship Eligibility

All riders who hold a current masters UCI license and UCI ID may ride in the Masters Pan American championships. However, the following riders are not eligible for the Masters Championship:

  1. Any rider who has ridden in the UCI cyclocross World Championships (Elite), Continental Championships, or UCI cyclocross World Cup during the current cyclocross season.
  2. Any rider, who has been a member, during the current cyclocross season, of a team registered with the UCI.
  3. Any rider classified with at least 100 points in the UCI individual cyclocross ranking published after the first UCI cyclocross world cup event of the current cyclocross season.

Note Regarding USA Cycling restrictions on Masters racers for USA National Championship events:

Any Masters racer who “Has a racing age of 30 years or older and has competed in any elite UCI World Cups, World Championships, Pan American Championship, Pan American or Olympic Games within the current calendar year MUST enter their respective Elite category.” 

 

Start Order and Start Procedures

Saturday

Pan American Continental Championships (except Masters)

The starting line staging area is located OFF COURSE before the start grid. Rider call-ups will begin approximately 10 minutes before the race starts. Riders not present for their call-up will lose their start grid position.

  2. Unclassified riders by random draw established by the commissaires

Confirm your ranking with the Race Secretary when you pick up your race number. Upon entering the call-up area, race officials will be checking the placement of your numbers and the width of your tires (33mm maximum).

The number of laps will be calculated and announced at the end of the second lap.

Masters Pan American Championships

  2. Existing PanAm Champion (within the current age group only)*
  3. Current masters national champion in their age category
  4. The rest of the first row: Top ranked riders from last year’s PanAm Results: Maximum of 8th place will be considered where those who did not change age brackets are considered “tied” with those who have aged up a bracket, with the tie-breaker going to the former.

Row 2, 3, 4:

SUBSEQUENT ROWS will not be conducted with a call-up procedure.

Feeding:

USAC Rule 4A15: Feeding is generally not permitted unless specifically authorized by the Chief Referee. If authorized, there is normally no feeding in the first two and final two laps of the race, and a temperature of at least 68 degrees is recommended. The location of feeding will be determined by the Chief Referee in conjunction with the Race Organization.

The riders undertake to respect nature and the environment throughout the course and not to pollute the site. The littering zone will be the pit area along its entire length. Waste must be deposited on the side of the course. It is strictly forbidden to throw waste directly onto the

course or outside the designated area. UCI 5.1.063 

 

For PanAm Championship events and UCI C2 races:

The act of handing out food or drinks is not allowed during cyclocross races. Nevertheless, a rider may keep and use food or drinks which they carry on their bikes or in their outfits. UCI 5.1.062 

 

Lapped Riders

For the UCI events, the 80% rule will be applied. The President of the Commissaire Panel will pull lapped riders if necessary. 

For the USA Cycling events: Lapped riders will finish on the same lap as the leaders. Riders in danger of being lapped must yield to oncoming racers and are not to interfere with their progress or trail behind them.

Local Food & Services Guide

On behalf of DCMTB, Crosshairs Cycling, and CXD Trek Bikes - Welcome to Washington DC! We are excited to be hosting the PanAmerican Cyclocross Championships and DCCX at the Armed Force Retirement Home. 

 

This city and region are great places to live, ride, and race. Check out this photo essay in the Radavist from friend of DCCX, Andy Karr of the Great Eskape, for more about the cycling communities and events in the city (including DCCX) that make this place special!

 

One of the biggest questions that bike racers and teams have when they come from out of town to a race and venue is where places to get food and groceries are located. This guide will direct you to places to eat and drink, nearby grocery stores close to the race venue, as well as the food trucks that will be at the venue so that racers, teams, supporters, and attendees can plan accordingly. 

 

We are grateful to be sponsored once again by Right Proper Brewing! We will be selling their beer at the race. Right Proper has two locations in DC - the Brookland Tasting Room and Right Proper Kitchen. Both Brookland locations are just a few minutes from the race venue and the new Right Proper Kitchen location in the Brookland ArtsWalk features a large outdoor patio perfect for hanging out after the racing is done!

 

Zeke’s Coffee of DC has been a longtime DCCX sponsor and we are happy to have them back as a sponsor as well as vendor for both days of racing. Visit them at their Rhode Island Ave NE Roastery/Coffee Shop or make the quick trip over to their Uptown Coffee Shop, less than a mile and a half from the race venue on 14th Street NW. If you land on a podium you might even take home a bag of Zeke's special DCCX Race Fuel coffee!

 

Acme Pie has been the official pie of DCCX for as long as we can remember! They have been a sponsor and a vendor for many years. Sol will be back once again this year serving pie to the hungry masses. Stop by the shop on Columbia Pike in Arlington VA if you are in town for an extra day to take pie home. 

 

We will have a number of food trucks on site during the race weekend. Below is the list of days and times they will be available:

  • TeaLoveBoba - Handcrafted drinks, including milk teas, fruits teas, and lemonade. Sat from 11am-4pm, Sun from 10am-5pm
  • TNT Mexican Grill -  Authentic Mexican street food including breakfast tacos. All day on Sat and Sun
  • Kush - Local cyclist Chef Ali’s unique Sudanese/Middle Eastern food truck. Sat and Sun after 11am
  • Blue Nile Burgers - Chef Ali’s take on classic burgers and loaded fries. Sun after 11am. 

 

Grocery Stores:

Safeway-Petworth - walking distance (¼ mile) to the venue on Georgia Ave. Open til midnight. Has a pharmacy. 

Yes Organic Market - like a smaller Whole Foods about half mile from the venue. 

Giant-Columbia Heights - a bit further (1.5 miles) but still close. Has a pharmacy. 

Trader Joes-Brookland - just opened, 2 miles from venue (1 hr free parking in garage on 8th St)

All above stores sell beer and wine.

 

Other services:

Two hardware stores nearby

  • Petworth ACE Hardware - less than a mile from the venue. 
  • Annie’s ACE Hardware - about 2 miles from the venue, near Trader Joe’s. 

CVS Pharmacy - on Georgia Ave about a half mile from the venue. 

Walmart - two Supercenters nearby if you need any last minute tents/race supplies:

  • Riggs Rd NE (just under 2 miles)
  • Georgia Ave NW (just over 2 miles)

Target-Columbia Heights - near the Giant, less than 2 miles from the venue in the DC USA complex. 

Georgia Ave/Petworth Metro station is at 3700 Georgia Ave NW Washington DC 20010, half mile walk or bike from the venue.

Loyalty Bookstore - one of the best local bookstores, just down the street at 9th and Upshur St NW. Open all weekend. 

Monroe Street Farmers Market at the Brookland Arts Walk. Sat from 9am-1pm. 2 miles from the race venue near Trader Joe’s, right next to the Brookland Metro (Red Line) and Met Branch Trail. 

 

Local Bike Shop & Ride Guide

We are thankful to be sponsored by Trek Bikes! We greatly appreciate Trek Clarendon (Arlington, VA) for providing neutral support for the race weekend. Go see Jeff Fraley and his team if you need service or parts before your big race. There are other Trek shops in the region -  check this list to find out where the closest Trek shop is if Trek Clarendon is not convenient.  There are two Trek stores in DC proper, Trek Skyland and Trek Georgetown.  

 

Arrow Bicycle in Hyattsville, MD, is about 5 miles from the race venue. They are a Trek dealer and are located along the Rhode Island Avenue Trolley Trail, near the Anacostia River Trail. An easy ride from the race venue!

 

There are two community bike shops within a few miles of the race venue. Highly recommended to stop in and learn more about what they do and grab a tube or any last minute bicycle need:

 

Gearin Up is a project of the Washington Area Bicyclist Association located in the Eckington neighborhood in NE DC, right off the Metropolitan Branch Trail (MBT). They are open until 7pm on Fridays and noon to 6pm on Saturdays. 

Upshift Workshop is an eclectic, woman-owned bicycle repair and education workshop in the Adams Morgan neighborhood in NW DC. They are open until  7pm on Fridays and noon-4pm on Saturdays and Sundays. 

 

If you are staying in the host hotel in the NoMA neighborhood, you’re just around the corner from DC’s flagship REI , adjacent to the NoMA Metro station (Red Line) and abutting the Metropolitan Branch Trail.

 

There are tons of places to ride in DC! The District Department of Transportation has a bicycle map that is worth looking at to familiarize yourself with bike lanes and trails in the city. You can find that map here.

 

Other places to ride:

The Metropolitan Branch Trail (MBT) is a multi-use trail that runs through the center of Washington, DC, connecting Union Station to (eventually) Silver Spring, MD. Most of the 8 miles are complete and there are protected bike lanes most of the way from the race venue to the trail access point in the Brookland neighborhood. Here are directions to the trail/two way protected cycletrack - hang a left at 8th St NE/Arts Walk to go up towards MD, hang a right to head downtown and Union Station. 

 

The Anacostia River Trail network starts in Maryland and continues into Washington, DC. Most of it is paved though there are sections of the NW Branch Trail that are dirt/singletrack (and perfect for cyclocross bikes if you like climbing). For info on the DC side, go here. For MD info, go here. 

 

Going for a bicycle ride in Rock Creek Park has been part of DC cycling life for decades. Junior World Road Championships were hosted there in 1978! This World Championship event was the first hosted in the US since 1912! If you want to relive that event, and see if you can better Greg LeMond’s 9th place finish, the race route is here.

 

North of Broad Branch Rd, much of Beach Drive is closed to car traffic so it is a great place to ride and explore. Only about two miles from the race venue is the Morrow Drive entrance to Rock Creek Park (at the Fitzgerald Tennis Center). At Beach Drive, make a right to head north towards Maryland and a left to head south towards Broad Branch and the Rock Creek trail which heads towards Georgetown and the National Mall (monuments, museums etc)

 

Sligo Creek Parkway has multiple road sections closed off to cars during the weekend, as well as a parallel multi-use trail. A great place to ride if you are staying north of DC in Silver Spring or Wheaton. More about Sligo Creek here. 

 

A bit further west are the paved Capital Crescent Trail and the unpaved C & O Canal Towpath. Both start in DC, in the Georgetown neighborhood, and meander into Maryland. 

 

DC does have legal singletrack! And cyclocross bikes fare pretty well on these trails. Learn more about the Ft Dupont and Ft Circle Park trails here. 

Last but not least is a favorite for those of us that live in the NE part of the city and Prince George’s County - the Beltsville Agricultural Research Center and the Patuxent Research Refuge. Miles of relatively low traffic roads. Take the Rhode Island Avenue Trolley Trail north and connect to Beaver Dam Rd and head east. Here are directions from the race venue.

EventName: Bison or Bust! The Tertiary Trek: National Bison Day Ride to Midewin National Tallgrass Prairie
EventNotes:
Public & Free

Hear Ye Hear Ye By way of bipartisan act of Congress and signed by President Obama into federal law, National Bison Day will be henceforth observed the first Saturday of every November! To celebrate this momentous occasion of the newly-dubbed “National Mammal” join a glorious mixed road & light gravel ride to a bison herd / obstinacy at Midewin National Tallgrass Prairie.

“Bison or Bust! The Tertiary Trek”
This remix of our inaugural 2024 ride is on the preserve’s 30th anniversary, for which they domesticated their roughest gravel segment. Lunch orders will be delivered to the bison preserve’s welcome center. Rendezvous include Metric Coffee (All), Blackberry Market (A & B), Jitters Cafe (All), Midewin Welcome Center (All), and The Junction vintage shop (All) for the after party. Everyone returns same-day to LaSalle St. Station by a specially-reserved Metra car. Before Joliet, anyone starting with “A” group can switch to “B” by just waiting. Everyone can switch to any other group at Jitters in Joliet, as well as the Midewin Welcome Center. Join our Strava club for updates!
 

“What are the ride rules?”

  • DO NOT PET THE FLUFFY COWS!
  1. All participants read, understand, and agree to the release / disclaimer / waiver at the bottom of the site before joining the ride
  2. Helmets required strapped onto your noggin’
  3. Bring a front and rear taillight as well as the tools, supplies, and know-how to change their own flats and address any mechanicals they may experience. From the 15th to 30th of October Comrade Cycles is offering free bike safety checks for our ride participants so get a checkup before the ride to cruise worry-free
  4. Observe best ride etiquette at all times: call out all slowing, stopping, speed bumps, holes, doors, cars, riders, runners, walkers, kids, turns, mechanicals, flats, gaps, and especially any pursuing buffaloes
  5. Keep your hands on your handlebars at all times, so flap your wings for rough roads instead of pointing. No riding without hands, we are too close together, roads are too unpredictable, and we have too far to go!
  6. Keep your eyes on the shoulders of the rider in front of you. They’ll call out and relay hazards as well as take the best line between them.
  7. That means if the rider ahead of you hits that minor road hole or whatever you do too, because it’s better than erratic unpredictable riding. No twitchy, racey, or unsafe group riding. There are plenty of other opportunities in other groups for that.
  8. No zooming in-between riders in peloton to make it three riders wide. Two wide? Stay that way. Single file? stay that way. It’s not a race, no need to jockey for position, and we will ask people to leave if they risk other riders’ safety
  9. Good vibes only! *All with good vibes are welcome* no matter their color shade, class, age, gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religion, profession, abilities, biking expertise, and strength.
  10. Good vibes only! That means no threatening or chauvinistic behavior of any kind is allowed be it racism, sexism, homophobia, classism, ethnic supremacism, or other forms of prejudice, threats, cruelty, or hatred nor are members of such ideologies permitted.
  11. No dangerous behavior is allowed and participants must follow all safety instructions of their ride leaders
  12. No unsolicited ‘coaching’ is allowed, especially any ‘helpful pushes’
  13. No triathlon aero handlebars are allowed they’re too unstable for the peloton
  14. No headphones
  15. Rides A and B require drop bars or something convincingly equivalent, like bullhorns. Point being that hybrid, flat, swoop, bull moose, albatross, wet noodle, whatever supercool other handlebars are only allowed for C group. This is just for safety in a peloton.
  16. No darting between riders. Is the peloton two riders wide? Keep it that way. Is it single-file? Keep it that way. Stay in your lane and ride with predictable behavior. This is not a race and anyone riding in ways that endanger others will be asked to find another ride.
  17. Join The ride Group appropriate for your abilities based on both practice and distance. Generally speaking, if you’ve been riding that distance in a week you’re ready to ride it in a day.
  18. Veteran brakeless fixed gear riders welcome but behind the peloton so pedal strikes don’t wipe others out.
  19. XXAndrew MichalskiXX or any other saboteurs

“What group should I join?”

For both Nachusa and Midewin routes the chillest group rolls at party pace, approximately 14mph, for around 40 miles. Both Midewin and Nachusa have a "B" group rolling for about 87 miles at 16-20mph once rolling. Both Midewin and Nachusa have an “A” group rolling at 18-24mph for about 130 miles. Whatever pace and distance you ride in a week you should able to do it in a day if you prepare well. Please practice riding in groups, calling out obstacles and "slowing" or "stopping" (see ride rules).

No groups are true drop rides. However, on “A” group we have a lot of miles to cover before dusk so if you have a really bad mechanical more involved than a flat, we must ask that you either link up with the next group riding by (when possible) or catch up at the next rendezvous by taking a shorter break to depart with us again. Study the routes and tabs atop the Ride With GPS event page carefully to make your choice. Keep in mind the ride is planned to be very adjustable:

  • Midewin Routes
    • Until Joliet, you can downgrade from "A" group by just waiting for "B" group.
    • You can change to any group at Jitters cafe in Joliet, and at the Midewin visitor's center.
    • Midewin Routes
      • Until Joliet we ride decently close to the train lines for the Heritage Corridor Metra train, but please keep in mind it does not run on weekends, and National Bison Day is always on the first Saturday of November. If you find yourself bonking your ejection seat lies on the Lincoln Service train home from Summit or Joliet, Carl Sandberg or Illinois Zephyr train home from La Grange, or in a ride share to the nearest Rock Island line Metra station, a line which begins at Joliet Gateway Station.

“What’s the timetable?”

TBA

“Do you have a waiver?”

Riding in groups and on roadways is extremely dangerous. Serious bodily injury and death can occur even when you and those around you are exercising extraordinary care. You must ride at your own risk. Thank you for being careful! By joining any of our rides all cyclists hereby release ride organizers, agents, sponsors, advertisers, partners, volunteers, affiliates and all other persons and entities from all liability. (Thanks Breakfast Club ATX!)

EventName: NICA Discovery- Warren, NJ Fall session 1
EventNotes:
We are so excited for your child to participate in NICA Discovery! 

 

All NICA Discovery adult leaders are background checked and hold a coaching license from NICA.  There will always be at least 2 leaders who have current first aid training. 

 

New Friends is the introductory level and is aimed at children who are new to biking but have some limited experience with neighborhood or urban riding.  These are children who can already balance and pedal a bike, but may have never ventured “off road.” Games and activities work on learning to better ride and operate a bike preparation for later buildable skills, and increasing stamina. 

 

Participants must be able to ride a bike without training wheels before joining a program and must be in 7-11 years old by program start date.

 

This session of NICA Discovery, Warren, NJ meets Saturdays 9:00 am-10:30

September 12

October 3

October 10

October 17

October 24

November 7

 

Required Documentation

ONLINE: 

  • Registration for NICA Discovery is through the platform BikeReg.  Go to bikereg.com and search “NICA Discovery” to find your location. 

IN PERSON: 

  • Parents must print, review this CODE OF CONDUCT with their child, sign and bring it to the first session for their child to participate. 
  • Every rider is also required to have a waiver and medical release form signed on file with NICA.  A link to the waiver may be found HERE.  Parents are asked to show confirmation that the online waiver has been signed before their child participates. 

Required Equipment

  • Helmet - Helmets should be less than 5 years old with no visible cracks or defects and fit your child’s head well without moving around while they ride. 
  • Footwear - Closed-toe (non-Croc like) shoes that fastened by laces, straps or buckles
  • Bike - Bike with knobby tires, gears, and two hand brakes. Bike tires should be no smaller than 20 inches.
  • Bike repair items - A replacement tube that fits your child’s tire. (dropped off at day one check in and returned at close of program if they are un-used.
  • Snug fitting small backpack  - Kids need to be able to carry water and snacks with them at all times.
  • Snacks/Hydration - Kids should always bring a snack and hydration with them to Discovery. 
    • Examples could include a granola bar, fruit snacks, or something that can easily be stored in a pocket or pack.
    • Hydration should consist of non caffeinated sports drinks or just good ole water! 

Recommended Equipment

  • Gloves - full-finger gloves to protect hands from abrasions in the case of a fall
  • Eye protection - generic sports glasses to protect from dust and debris (and bugs) kicked up while riding
  • Windbreaker /rain jacket/coat - weather conditions change throughout the season, your child should be prepared to ride in the conditions that are present on the day. Sessions will be altered or canceled if the weather conditions are unsafe. 
  • Athletic /Cycling pants- Loose fitting athletic pants. Cycling specific shorts are not required but some kids may be more comfortable.

What to Expect

Each lesson is broken down into 3 sections.  

  • Opener activities and objective/expectation setting
  • Skills activities and Games 
  • Wrap up and Reflection

There will be a  break mid-lesson for snacking/hydrating and general check in.

Each lesson builds on skills learned in the previous one.  To get the MOST out of NICA Discovery make sure your child can attend every lesson! 

For New Friends, the lessons consist of riding and playing in a park-like setting and are not trail dependent. Students will ride within that open space rather than out on trails, staying close to restroom facilities and support. 

 

Kids should come ready to learn, play, ride and explore!

Backpack examples 

A small pack that fits snugly and is just big enough to carry a water bottle and snacks, and maybe a small found treasure or two is great.

Helmet examples

Bike examples 

Guide to Kids' Bike Sizing

How to determine if the bike is the correct size

While straddling the bike with feet flat on the ground, the rider should have about 2 inches of clearance between the top tube and their inseam.

Here is a statement regarding e-bike rules and regulations for the Threat Level Midnight Event:

Threat Level Midnight Event: E-Bike Rules and Regulations

To address inquiries regarding e-bike eligibility for the bike categories at the Threat Level Midnight Event, we are following the basic rules adopted by USA Cycling for competitive electric bicycle events.

The electric bikes permitted for competition are defined as Pedelecs" (pedal electrics), which utilize both pedaling and electric power.

For the Threat Level Midnight Event, we are adopting the Class 1 e-bike definition as the standard for entry. This ensures fair and regulated competition and aligns with the Consumer Products Safety Council guidelines:

Class 1 E-Bike Requirements:

No Throttle: The bike must not have a throttle mechanism.
Pedaling System:Must have a freely operable pedaling system (rear-wheel drivetrain of pedals, crank, chain, and gear system).
Motor Power:750 watts or less motor power (manufacturer's label of compliance is the minimum standard).
Motor Engagement: Motor assistance engages only when the rider is actively pedaling.
Motor Cut-Off: Motor assistance cuts off at a maximum speed of 20 mph (32 km/h).

Additional Allowable Options:

Battery: A single battery is permitted.
Start Assist: Limited start assist (without pedaling) is allowed up to a maximum speed of 4 mph (6 km/h).

Participants are responsible for ensuring their e-bike meets these specifications prior to the event. Compliance checks will be made. We look forward to seeing you at the start line!

 

Events are subject to weather and trail conditions. Helmets must be worn at all times while riding. Promoter reserves the right to cancel/reschedule the event. Promoter reserves the right to change start times and distances if needed. For more info or questions please email: events@missourioffroadcyclists.com

 

Funds raised go to support the Missouri Off Road Cyclists, a regional non-profit advocating for, building, maintaining, and preserving sustainable multi-use soft surface trails throughout Southwest Missouri.

Please visit our website for venue information and racing requirements. https://www.utcx.net

UTCX is a USA Cycling-sanctioned series and follows USA Cycling’s Competition Category Policy.

Any UTCX category that is not designated as a Women’s or Junior category is open to all riders, regardless of sex assigned at birth. For the 2026 season, this gives riders 10 categories open to everyone, subject to the age and USA Cycling category requirements listed for each race.

Women’s categories follow USA Cycling’s eligibility requirements. Junior categories are based on age and sex category.

Our goal is simple: there is a place for everyone to race at UTCX, and all riders are welcome.

Welcome to the 30th season of the NCCX series.  We are excited to have you racing. This season's race schedule has a few changes.  If you have questions at the races, please look for our friendly NCCX Ambassadors located at registration and around the race course. From beginner to experienced racers, there are opportunities for all to participate and compete. 

Registration- All registrations will be online. There is a discount for pre-registration, and we encourage everyone to choose this option. Early registration discount ends on Thursday night for all Saturday races, and Friday night for all Sunday races. Race day registration is available and will be online via your mobile device. 

Race Numbers- If you did not participate in the first race of the season, you must purchase a 2026 race number; the race number fee is included in registration. If you have a 2026 race number, a discount will be applied to your entry fee. Please save your number and adhere your timing chips carefully to the top of your helmet. Race numbers are made of fabric and will be used throughout the season. If you lose or forget your race number, there is a $5 replacement fee.

Refunds of registration- There will be no registration refunds.

Your racing age is your age as of December 31, 2027 (this is cyclocross after all).

All fields will be scored separately.

First 2 rows of riders pre-registered by 8PM the day before the event will receive call-ups based on Cross Results rankings.  Riders will be separated into groups by start time within each wave.

Staging will begin 10 mins prior to each race.

In-person registration opens at 9:00 AM and closes 15 minutes before the start of each race.

Lapped riders will finish on the same lap as the leader.  Riders in danger of being lapped must yield to oncoming racers and may not interfere with their progress.

Helmets are required for all riders on bicycles, even when not actively racing.  Radios, iPods, MP3 players, earphones, etc. are NOT allowed while racing.  

Please do not enter the course while a race is in progress.  The course official will announce when pre-riding of the course is allowed.  Riders entering the course for pre-riding must do so after the finish line and only after the "course is open' announcement has been made.  

Zip ties, limit screw mods, battery removal, and honor code pinky swearing for single-speed racers are allowed and encouraged.

Additional same-day races are $10 (free for Juniors 18 and under).  

The promoter and/or race officials reserve the right to modify, combine, or cancel races in the event of insufficient entries, dangerous weather conditions or other emergencies beyond their control.

No cash payouts for any heats.  In an effort to make the races more accessible and inclusive we are reducing entry fees to bare minimum required to cover race day costs!

EventNotes:
Ride your bike. Win a bike!

Make a difference.

That's what Lititz Bikeworks' Cranksgiving is all about. It costs absolutely nothing to register and you get so much in return. Like the ride itself. You'll love the scenic spin through the most beautiful Amish farmland in Lancaster County, including covered bridges and the fall foliage along the WERT rail trail. All we ask is that you purchase non-perishables at each grocery stop along the route.

Brought to you by Stauffers of Kissel Hill grocery stores. 

This year we have two routes available for you to ride;  A 30-mile rolling route stopping at three grocery stores, and for those who want a hilly challenge there is a 40 mile Covered Bridge option that stops at one grocery store.  There will be a donation area at each grocery store where you can place your purchases (no worries about carrying them with you on your ride. The goal here is to feed as many families as possible, not to weigh you down!).

This year, Cranksgiving is continuing our reach and will benefit two non-profit organizations that connect people in need with resources; Manheim Central Food Pantry and Ephrata Area Social Services. We're so impressed with the heart and soul of these local organizations, each does so much for local families. The ride this year is brought to you by Stauffers of Kissel Hill. For over 80 years, they have been offering customers high quality food, home and garden products, and services in central Pennsylvania under the brand that has become known as Stauffers of Kissel Hill.

There will be a mass start at 9:00am, and Collusion Tapworks will be serving up hot sandwiches, sides and cold beers at Lititz Bikeworks from 11-1. We are giving away a gravel bike at the end of the day, so enter the raffle and stay for the drawing!

We can't wait to ride with you on November 7th!

-The team at Lititz Bikeworks and our gracious sponsor, Stauffers of Kissel Hill

EventNotes:
AllFor1Endurance Challenge is a multi-sport endurance challenge 100% for charity.  IT IS NOT A RACE.  AF1Endurance is an event by which athletes of different sport can come together on the same day for adventure and to raise awareness and financial support for the charities that AF1Endurance advocates for.    There is NO FEE to register, however, AF1Endurance is built with athlete-driven fundraising at its core.  Every registrant will have his/her own fundraising platform through PledgeReg by which they can make their own donations and build a team of sponsors by sending friends and family, coworkers and businesses a personal PledgeReg link so that they too can donate on the athlete's behalf!  There are no winners or losers in the AF1Endurance, no timing, no podium, HOWEVER, to elevate the two main drives of AF1 (challenge and charity) the athletes who meet all of the following criteria will receive a finisher's medal:

  1. among the first 100 athletes to register
  2. finish their course
  3. make a minimum $100 donation to an AF1-supported charity

All athletes will receive a small gesture of our appreciation for participating in the first annual AF1Endurance Challenge. Some participants will also receive specially-made local wood-turned trophies to be given to a small number of athletes who particularly emulate the spirit of AF1.  These individuals need not be among the first to register, and because AF1Endurance is not a race, they may not be the athlete who you'd expect to get a trophy… you'll just have to come out and see… maybe it'll be YOU!

Further information on all the above and more can and will be found as its posted on the AllFor1Endurance Instagram page!  Registrant athletes will receive an email with links for further pertinent resources, such as maps, their PledgeReg account, and other event-related details. 

Head to Instagram now to view posts, reels, and highlighted stories about the event, videos like this one give a sneak peek to the fun adventure that awaits: https://www.instagram.com/p/Dbm_kQoM3V7/

Excited to take this first step in a leap of faith to be All For 1!!

-TeamAF1

Prepare for an amazing cycling experience in a beautiful area of Texas!  Long known by some for its amazing cycling, the Leakey area is surrounded by hills and canyons with the famous Frio River winding its way through the heart of this Texas gem.  

 

We're giving you an adventure onto private ranches, backroads, and trails along the Frio River with views of stunning towering cliffs, springs, and waterfall as you ride along singletrack and ranch access trails.  You also get to ride brand new fast rolling mountain bike/running trails right on the edge of town.  Connecting everything together, is quiet rolling chipseal roads and challenging gravel roads with even more views of the hills surrounding the Frio River.  Take your choice of 35 or 50 miles for a great day of riding.  This is a DON'T MISS event with three different surfaces, with dirt/caliche/chipseal (The Texas Three Step), that will have you thinking about the best equipment to bring!

 

Choose your ride wisely!  Any bike with a minimum of 40mm (40c) wide tires will work for this event, and bigger will be even better!  It is possible that a mountain bike will have the most fun for this one.  Tubeless tires with sealant is strongly recommended, and the ability to navigate with GPS on a bike computer or Ride With GPS app enabled smartphone on the handlebar is required.

 

This event is not timed, and is not a race, but we know many like to go fast.  Take it fast if you like, but keep your head up to enjoy the amazing sights!  For the party pacers, you are going to have a fantastic morning of riding and experiences!

 

At the finish line party, we'll have music, included lunch and drink waiting for you and all your friends at the Rustic Frio venue right on the county courthouse square.  Lunch is provided by the Leakey Lions Club and will benefit their community service programs in the Leakey area!

 

This event benefits local businesses, non-profits, and landowners, and helps increase access to cycling in the area!  And it's going to be an incredible ride experience that will have you telling everyone about it for a long time!
